name: Andy Matthews
subject: Endorsement alert
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ANDY FOR NEVADA
body:
Our campaign continues to build momentum... | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/andyfornevada/friday-weekly-5859805?e=6736d7bc47)
---
| | [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/1A73L5b9mmZ?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)
---
| | Dear Peter,

I’ve got some big news for you today, my friend. The state’s largest newspaper, the _Las Vegas Review-Journal_ , has announced it is endorsing me in my re-election campaign for Nevada Controller.

Here’s what the _RJ_ ’s editors write:

_Mr. Matthews, who previously served two years in the Assembly, has represented Nevada well as its chief fiscal officer. He is a stalwart proponent of transparency and created the “state checkbook,” which allows taxpayers to access online detailed information on state outlays. He hopes to use his second term to persuade local governments to do the same. Mr. Matthews has also championed the creation of a state inspector general to conduct forensic audits of state departments in search of waste or fraud. He favors subjecting public-sector collective bargaining to the open meeting law, an excellent idea. ..._

_Voters should enthusiastically support**Andy Matthews.**_

You can read the full write-up [here](https://us.list-manage.com/czCUF7KMyuF?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73).

I’m honored to receive the paper’s endorsement, which is just the latest of many as my campaign continues to build strong momentum for these final weeks. Earlier, I was honored to receive the endorsements of the [Vegas Chamber](https://us.list-manage.com/1D6B1WpRuku?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) and the [Latin Chamber of Commerce](https://us.list-manage.com/hdncUGisdPK?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73), as well as Citizens for Responsible Government, Nevada Right to Life, and others. Nevada’s Independent American Party has also announced it’s recommending me for re-election.

By the way, I wanted to let you know we’ve also launched a couple of new TV ads highlighting my commitment to government transparency. The ads are similar, as you’ll notice, and we’re targeting them at swing voters in Nevada’s two largest counties.

[This one](https://us.list-manage.com/DjK1CH9CIA8?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) is running in Washoe County, touting my work in helping local leaders put their county checkbook online.

And [this one](https://us.list-manage.com/173SoMlYzo4?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) is running in Clark County, and includes my pledge to work with leaders to do the same there in my second term.

We’re trying to get these ads in front of as many eyeballs as possible, and so I hope you’ll consider a contribution to help us do exactly that.

[You can contribute by clicking here.](https://us.list-manage.com/4ZQWyiECKGI?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)

Well, that’s all for now. As always, thank you for standing with me in my fight to make Nevada’s government more transparent and accountable to the hard-working taxpayers like you who fund it.

Take care, and I’ll see you next time!

For Nevada’s future,

Andy

name: James Carville
subject: New Hampshire is a coin flip [MEMO]
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9471%2E582294%2ELz6j6E ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9471%2E582294%2ELz6j6E ]Chris Pappas for Senate

Hi. It's
James Carville.

I've been sounding the alarm about New Hampshire for months. I said Chris
Pappas’s race was being ignored. I said the math didn't work without it. I
said John Sununu was a uniquely dangerous opponent.

Now we’ve got just days to go, and the polls are all over the map. One has
Sununu ahead. One has it dead even. One has Pappas up. That tells me one
thing: This race is anyone's game.

I put together an urgent memo to explain what that means. Read it right
now. Then help Chris Pappas win this thing.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261011_3.artdyQ&refcode=em20261010-3&t=1003&akid=9471%2E582294%2ELz6j6E ]If you don't need convincing, rush a $5 donation to Chris
Pappas's campaign immediately.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261011_3.artdyQ&amount=5&refcode=em20261010-3&t=1004&akid=9471%2E582294%2ELz6j6E ]Donate $5 »

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

OCTOBER 2026 CAMPAIGN MEMO ON NH-SEN

FROM: James Carville, Senior Democratic Strategist
TO: Interested Parties

I need to be clear with you about where things stand in the race for New
Hampshire's open Senate seat. This race is a coin flip, and it is going to
stay that way until the very last vote is cast.

The polls are a mixed bag, and that should worry every Democrat.

* The University of New Hampshire's Granite State Poll had John Sununu
ahead of Chris Pappas in August, 45% to 43%.
* And in September, it was a total mixed bag:

* Republicans' own polling for the National Republican Senatorial
Committee had Sununu up by a point, 37% to 36%.
* A co/efficient poll had the race tied at 46% apiece.
* The New York Times/Siena poll had Pappas up 50% to 45%.

* Put those together, and you don't get a frontrunner. You get a race
that could go either way, and Republicans know it.

The GOP's investment in this race keeps growing.

* Some $60 million+ in outside money has already flooded New Hampshire
to boost Sununu and attack Pappas. That's in a state with fewer than
one million registered voters. Voters are getting absolutely hammered
with Republican ads.

* The Senate Leadership Fund has announced $17 million for Sununu.
* A Trump-aligned super PAC has reserved another $10 million in New
Hampshire ads.
* Koch-backed Americans for Prosperity Action has already spent
over $15 million.

* John Sununu is not a back-bench candidate. He has a famous New
Hampshire political name (his father and his brother both served as
governor), he has won a statewide election here before, and he has the
full weight of the Republican donor machine behind him.
* Republicans understand the math perfectly. They don't need to flip
five seats like we do. They just need to flip New Hampshire red and
make Democrats' path to a majority impossible.

In New Hampshire almost nobody has voted yet.

* In states around the country, voters are already casting their
ballots. New Hampshire is different.
* There's no early in-person voting here, and absentee voting requires
an excuse. Roughly nine in ten Granite Staters cast their ballots in
person on Election Day itself.
* New Hampshire also has same-day voter registration. In 2024 nearly
93,000 people registered at the polls on Election Day.
* That means this race is not even close to decided. Nearly every vote
that will decide it is still out there, and every one of them is still
up for grabs. We have to stay vigilant.

New Hampshire has decided control before — and the margins are razor thin.

* In 2016 the New Hampshire Senate race was decided by just 1,017 votes.
* When Democrats chart a path to retaking the Senate majority, New
Hampshire is not optional. If Chris Pappas loses, Democrats need to
flip five seats instead of four. That math does not exist.

Races like this are won in the final weeks.

* I have worked Senate races in every corner of this country. And I can
tell you from hard experience: When a race is this close, it gets
decided by the side that shows up in the final stretch with the
resources to finish strong.
* In New Hampshire the final stretch is everything. When nearly the
whole electorate votes on one day, the last ad they see and the last
door that gets knocked matter more than anywhere else in the country.
* I am telling you right now: Chris Pappas can win this race. But only
if we give him what he needs to compete between now and November 3rd.

Chris Pappas has what it takes to win — but he needs resources right now.

* Pappas has won New Hampshire's 1st Congressional District four times
without a loss. He just won his primary with 65% of the vote. He knows
how to reach voters across the aisle and build a coalition that wins.
* Pappas has outraised Sununu candidate-to-candidate, thanks to support
from hundreds of thousands of individual donors. But that advantage
gets swallowed up fast when $60 million in outside money is hitting
the airwaves.
* In a race that could come down to a few thousand votes, being drowned
out on TV in the final weeks is the ballgame. We are in that moment
right now.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Listen.
I don't write memos like this for every race, and I don't send urgent
updates unless I'm genuinely worried.

I'm telling you: I'm worried about New Hampshire.

The polls are split. Republicans are spending like crazy. And almost every
vote in this race is still waiting to be cast.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261011_3.artdyQ&refcode=em20261010-3&t=1005&akid=9471%2E582294%2ELz6j6E ]Rush a donation to Chris Pappas immediately. Don't let New Hampshire be
the race we wish we'd done more for when we had the chance.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261011_3.artdyQ&amount=5&refcode=em20261010-3&t=1024&akid=9471%2E582294%2ELz6j6E ]Donate $5 »

Right now is our time to play ball. Let's elect Chris Pappas and flip the
Senate.

– James Carville

_Rick and Conor talk Trump and the 2026 campaign_
Rick Telesz is a retired dairy farmer who lives north of Pittsburgh. He is both a lifelong Democrat and someone who voted for Trump. Having long realized he was "conned," Rick decided to run for the statehouse this year as a Democrat. In Pennsylvania, the Democrats control the state house by one seat, and they don't control the state Senate -- so races like Rick's are vitally important. While this is normally a tough seat for us to win, Rick's Republican opponent, the incumbent Aaron Bernstine, was recently stripped of his committees in Harrisburg because of a [homophobic outburst](https://substack.com/redirect/1f1530f2-6b32-42c7-94a4-a50cfb73c920?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The news coverage around the scandal has injected new life into Rick's campaign and brought victory within reach.
You can support Rick [here](https://substack.com/redirect/7f261792-595f-4222-9198-7a6c8184b501?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In a race like this one, which could be decided by a few hundred votes, even small donations make an enormous difference. They can help Rick get extra signs and palm cards in the closing weeks, which might give him just enough name recognition to get over the top in this rural district. I try not to bother you too often on behalf of candidates, but Rick is exactly the kind of person we need serving in public office. He's honest, humble, and has no agenda other than to try to make life more affordable for the next generation. He also happens to be a more credible voice on agriculture than we normally have on our side. It would be an enormous achievement to elect him this fall.
Thank you and Happy Sunday!

Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to flip Congress in 23 days. If you need help checking your voter registration or making a plan to vote, please visit [iwillvote.com](https://ak.democrats.org/go/9784?t=1&akid=9824%2E22930333%2EJTkQrq). 1% and 0.3%

Peter, those two
numbers are why we can’t get comfortable, no matter how good the energy
feels on the ground.

1% is Abdul's primary margin of victory. 0.3% is Senator Elissa Slotkin's
margin of victory when she beat the same opponent, Mike Rogers, in 2024.
That came down to just 20,217 votes.

So no matter what the polls or betting markets say, or how many rooms we
fill up across Michigan, we have to keep campaigning like we're 10 points
down.

Just like in the primary, we're up against millions of dollars in outside
spending:

* By Election Day, MAGA Republicans will likely have spent $100 million
in Michigan alone.

* They’ve reserved over $1 million a day from here on to pummel us with
attack ads and boost Mike Rogers.

That’s why we can’t relax even for a second. But we don't need to be
scared, either.

Organizing can beat that kind of money. We proved it in the primary, and
we will prove it again this November so long as we stick together.

Reaching enough voters to overcome a $100 million campaign to stop us
costs more than what we have sitting in the bank right now.
Peter, we
urgently need more resources to host events, run ads, and talk to voters
across Michigan.

Team, Did you see this? Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth just announced that our military’s cyber forces – the U.S. Cyber Command – will work with the Department of Homeland Security to defend our elections from any foreign interference. But Trump has gutted critical election security infrastructure since he entered the White House – including the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) that was designed to ensure our elections are free, fair, and safe. _As one expert put it:_ | | | _**“If the administration was serious about assisting state and local election officials, they shouldn’t have dismantled all of the federal government’s election cybersecurity capacity and fired all their experts in early 2025.”** \- Former DOJ Attorney David Becker_
---|---|---
This is the same administration that has pushed countless conspiracy theories about our election system – that Trump won the 2020 election, that our elections are "rigged" against him and MAGA Republicans, and that there's widespread voter fraud.
So with the midterms approaching, voters have every right to ask what this announcement is really about – and whether putting a close Trump ally like Pete Hegseth in charge of "watching" our elections will protect them or put them at risk.
**Democratic Secretaries of State are the ones standing between voters and these attacks. Their job is to make sure every eligible person can vote, and make sure every vote counts.**

Friend, We live in the richest country in the world: No one should go hungry, or go bankrupt from medical emergencies, or die because they can’t get healthcare. **But Trump’s Big Brutal Bill cuts are coming into effect, and life’s about to get a lot less affordable for families who’ve already been struggling to afford the basics.** If you use SNAP or Medicaid, or if you get your health insurance from your state’s ACA marketplace or exchange, please know that rising costs and requirements are coming up. I’ve included more details after my signoff below. These Republican-led cuts and obstacles to accessing life-saving needs are intentionally disruptive and harmful to individuals, states, and local communities. [**Lives are at stake. _Here’s more information about changes from Trump’s Brutal Bill that are happening this month and the next few months:_
> **More recipients of SNAP food assistance will now face more requirements** to work, volunteer, or go to school for more time to be able to keep their benefits — including people who are 55-64 years old, people with 14-17 year-old children, and unhoused people. To keep their benefits, people will also need to**manually renew their SNAP**(food stamps), which may have different names depending on the state.
> Administrative costs for SNAP are also going up, and now the **federal government is forcing states to pay even more than before to administer SNAP to their residents.** Some states will not be able to pay; some will pass this cost to struggling local governments.
> Refugees and some other previously eligible non-citizens are **losing access to SNAP and**** _Affordable Care Act_****(ACA) subsidies** , which help cover the cost of health insurance. Some immigrants will also face more challenges and restrictions when trying to access Medicaid, CHIP, and Medicare.
> **Re-enrollment and open enrollment is coming up for people who get their health insurance through their state’s exchange or marketplace** , which was set up by the Affordable Care Act.
> **Please pay attention in this year’s re-enrollment period:** Some people will get a smaller ACA subsidy, some people’s subsidies will be cancelled, and some states are dropping certain plans. You may need to change your plan, which may affect which of your prescriptions or providers are covered. Some people will be forced to drop their plan — priced out of health insurance, as millions were over the past year.
> And starting in January, Medicaid recipients will need to provide their eligibility every six months, and work reporting requirements will also get stricter. Some states are unfortunately tightening up work reporting requirements earlier than is necessary.
These changes are outrageous, but I want to make sure you’re informed. I promise to keep fighting for you and for families in need.

clean_body: As prices rise and federal assistance shrinks, families urgently need more support. | | | Friend, We live in the richest country in the world: No one should go hungry, or go bankrupt from medical emergencies, or die because they can’t get healthcare. But Trump’s Big Brutal Bill cuts are coming into effect, and life’s about to get a lot less affordable for families who’ve already been struggling to afford the basics. If you use SNAP or Medicaid, or if you get your health insurance from your state’s ACA marketplace or exchange, please know that rising costs and requirements are coming up. I’ve included more details after my signoff below. These Republican-led cuts and obstacles to accessing life-saving needs are intentionally disruptive and harmful to individuals, states, and local communities. | Thank you. Healthcare and food are human rights that are necessary for life, not privileges reserved for those who can afford it. With you in the fight for our rights and our lives, Rashida Here’s more information about changes from Trump’s Brutal Bill that are happening this month and the next few months: More recipients of SNAP food assistance will now face more requirements to work, volunteer, or go to school for more time to be able to keep their benefits — including people who are 55-64 years old, people with 14-17 year-old children, and unhoused people. To keep their benefits, people will also need tomanually renew their SNAP(food stamps), which may have different names depending on the state. Administrative costs for SNAP are also going up, and now the federal government is forcing states to pay even more than before to administer SNAP to their residents. Some states will not be able to pay; some will pass this cost to struggling local governments. Refugees and some other previously eligible non-citizens are losing access to SNAP and** Affordable Care Act(ACA) subsidies , which help cover the cost of health insurance. Some immigrants will also face more challenges and restrictions when trying to access Medicaid, CHIP, and Medicare. Re-enrollment and open enrollment is coming up for people who get their health insurance through their state’s exchange or marketplace , which was set up by the Affordable Care Act. Please pay attention in this year’s re-enrollment period: Some people will get a smaller ACA subsidy, some people’s subsidies will be cancelled, and some states are dropping certain plans. You may need to change your plan, which may affect which of your prescriptions or providers are covered. Some people will be forced to drop their plan — priced out of health insurance, as millions were over the past year. And starting in January, Medicaid recipients will need to provide their eligibility every six months, and work reporting requirements will also get stricter. Some states are unfortunately tightening up work reporting requirements earlier than is necessary. These changes are outrageous, but I want to make sure you’re informed. I promise to keep fighting for you and for families in need. \---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Rashida Tlaib** Date: Sat, Oct 10, 2026 Subject: Tell Congress: Reverse cuts to SNAP, Medicaid, and ACA assistance, and pass policies for universal healthcare and school meals To: dpwillis67@gmail.com Friend, Some of Trump’s Big Brutal Bill cuts aregoing into effect this month and in the coming months. If you use SNAP, Medicaid, CHIP (the Children's Health Insurance Program), or Affordable Care Act (ACA) subsidies to make your health insurance more affordable, please check out the overview of information below the first hyperlink. Republicans’ cuts to federal nutrition and healthcare programs were the deepest in our country’s history, stripping life-saving assistance from millions of Americans and their families. And more are to come, unless Congress acts. With millions of families already struggling to afford basic needs such as food and healthcare, and prices on the rise, we must demand Congress act soon. Here are the changes happening this month and the next few months, by early 2027: Many recipients of SNAP food assistance now face more requirements to work, volunteer, or go to school for more time to be able to keep their benefits — including people who are 55-64 years old, people with 14-17 year-old children, and unhoused people. People will also need tomanually renew their SNAP(food stamps), which may have different names depending on your state. The costs of administering SNAP are also going up, and now the federal government is forcing states to pay even more than before to administer SNAP to their residents. Some states can’t pay; some will pass along this cost to struggling local governments. (My state of MI has set aside and approved $170 million for this, but that money could be invested in our communities in other ways, such as building affordable housing and getting lead out of our water.) In addition, some previously eligible non-citizens (like refugees) are losing access to SNAP and** Affordable Care Act(ACA) subsidies that help cover the cost of health insurance. And for some immigrants, it will be even harder to access Medicaid, CHIP, and Medicare. If you get ACA subsidies for your health insurance through your state’s exchange or marketplace, please pay attention in this year’s re-enrollment period: Some people will get a smaller subsidy, some people’s subsidies will be cancelled, and some states are dropping certain plans — so you may need to change your plan, which may affect which of your prescriptions or providers are covered. Work reporting requirements for Medicaid eligibility are also going up in every state by next January, when people will also need to prove their eligibility every 6 months. In the richest country in the world, no one should go hungry, go bankrupt from medical emergencies, or die because they can’t get healthcare. Thank you for continuing to push our leaders to serve the American people, and to move with the urgency that our communities deserve. Instead of spending more on war than any other country in the world, we need to invest in our people’s urgent needs. Together we’ll keep pushing more lawmakers to support transformative programs. We’ll keep trying to fix the affordability crisis and guarantee our human rights to food, healthcare, housing, and beyond. With you in the fight for better, Rashida Rashida Tlaib for Congress PO Box 32777 Detroit, MI 48232 | Paid for by Rashida Tlaib for Congress | | Sent via . name: Nick Shirley
subject: A law with my name on it?
body:

That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. clean_body: I found the fraud, now I'm the target The dubbed "Stop Nick Shirley Act" was made to stop me. | | | | | | | Friend, There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law actually does. Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Friend: it makes it harder for anyone -- me included -- to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent. I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; this is just the beginning. Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General -- the one person in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Friend. That's the system protecting itself. I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. They're right -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Friend: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, Lincoln Media Foundation was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation. They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the first place. I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them. Since LMF is a 501(c)3, your gift is tax-deductible , and it can be made anonymously if that's what you'd prefer. Friend, they can pass all the laws they want. They can try to prevent people like me from exposing their corruption, that's why it crucial to support independent journalists like myself. They are creating laws to silence free speech -- and that's why we need to continue the fight and I need your support. People like you decide this work is worth funding, and it helps me continue! For the truth, Nick Shirley P.S. -- A California assemblyman is already asking the DOJ to intervene against this law. | | | | Peter, If you want to know exactly how the federal government is managing the lands _you_ own, just follow the money. In Minnesota, the Trump administration is aggressively pushing to allow a toxic sulfide-ore mine right next to the pristine Boundary Waters. The foreign mining company getting the green light **just happens to be owned by a Chilean billionaire who provides a luxury residence to the President’s daughter.** It turns out the going rate for risking the most visited wilderness area in the United States is a nice rental property. You really can't make this stuff up. [**Before we go on, can we count on you to pitch in $3 or more today to our October rapid-response war chest so we can drag these corrupt backroom deals into the light?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/87N0wZz-DvE_jtmVXc-_3Q~~/AAUS1hA~/zYns1q6XPg69sfX9tvZPcn3RfASt8vewYhelmGL50ENGVKfQe_0ZWLC2EI62ZRyXnoQXCh6X04iU-XTBSByUBNSqB9JDBqX1eQR7rEBDBlxbZ8xmbfBiBfFfzrdmKV4uuFMinLaWEiFaHU9CkiEJin4JXrUOqNFR0AbHkR527_slb_fHHbSlyRTf96ihNDG7jqjAAa7CL-z2C93NZie8rswbtNqK4Vw6JKTMpSJ5B0YN-XPmy4jyee5pB3E-113L) **[**DONATE »** ](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/vsKjKZb4mhdt6gMo73PF3Q~~/AAUS1hA~/WQxPWK_4gFe2_UXk4Se5rLpLNUGRj_M1eL3pXo-OHcp2XJy8XreMiEsf8VE6FhO-8mbxlmm-S1oPdWX2e9gFuEHywToiex7s511qepLjNqMkwU6rJ4svXTI5cUlol0Evs6aC0tCYsOd23nzqcquozm7eIdFUlHST4KU1hBk11kClZHAj47DgYVEQXo90j7qihqywEADafc5u2D_JC3wQGywa7rFkKDZJyMrkMz2pGrPUcokHPamhb5HdZgLTn7TR) ** The Boundary Waters is just the tip of the spear. The sheer scale of the theft they are attempting across the country is staggering:
* **Out West:** They slashed Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante by 90% so mining executives could immediately stake uranium claims on sacred archaeological sites.
* **In our National Forests:** They repealed the Roadless Rule, stripping protections from 45 million acres of untouched landscapes just so the timber lobby can clear-cut the backcountry.
* **Down South:** They are waiving environmental laws to bulldoze through sensitive ecosystems, decimating Organ Pipe National Monument and threatening Big Bend for a vanity border wall.

They are robbing us of our national heritage and expecting us to just sit back and take it. They think their billionaire backers have already bought this victory, and they believe they’re untouchable. **We have exactly 62 days until Election Day to prove them wrong.** At Public Land Warriors, we aren't just writing polite letters of complaint. We are building a targeted, inescapable digital ad blitz to hit the airwaves in the home districts of the politicians who are cheering on this destruction. We are going to offer a very clear perspective to the voters in their districts: exactly who these politicians sold them out to. _**by[Lawrence Winnerman](https://substack.com/redirect/a29a325f-f60c-4309-aeb1-98ff21edc8a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
_**Cliff 's Note:**_
##### A guy with an AI subscription built free clones of seven Adobe apps in about a week. Lawrence Winnerman spent twenty-five years inside Microsoft and Amazon, and he knows exactly what this is: Napster, round two. He's also seen who walked away with the money last time.
##### That's the kind of insider read your subscription pays for. [Through November 3, a year of Blue Amp Media is 30 percent off. Join us at blueamp.co/subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/d6fb8814-0a0c-4c56-9df3-780592e57fba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.CICI9SWEIUX5S_N7qnzsxYoIIIHWoKSxnfU9ivcrdbw?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=219880115)
_**-- Cliff**_
* * *
On September 30, a developer named Brandon Thomas started posting code to GitHub. Within a week he had 7 repositories up, each a free, open-source stand-in for an Adobe product: Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat. He wrote them in Rust, a coding language, with Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, a model that had been on sale for 8 days when he started. He says he "one-shotted Photoshop." That means he gave the AI tool one detailed instruction, and then let it run until it was complete. Adobe charges $69.99 a month for the suite. The clones cost nothing.
For now, they are also kind of a mess. The Gaussian blur in the Photoshop clone misbehaves, and the project's own README admits it is "not yet a Photoshop replacement for daily professional work." Adobe will lean on that sentence for as long as it stays true. I give it until Thanksgiving.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d6fb8814-0a0c-4c56-9df3-780592e57fba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Eric S. Raymond, the open-source elder, looked at the repos and guessed Thomas must have decompiled Adobe's code, turned it into a specification, and had the machine write fresh Rust from the spec. "Adobe just got nuked," he wrote. "And closed source is dead, dead, dead." The project says otherwise. It calls itself a clean-room reimplementation, built from public specifications and observed behavior, with no Adobe code anywhere in it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d6fb8814-0a0c-4c56-9df3-780592e57fba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
People have argued all week about which version is true, and the argument misses what matters, because the clean-room version is the scarier one for Adobe. Clean-room cloning has been legal in this country for 40 years. In the early 1980s, Compaq spent about $1 million having one team describe what IBM's BIOS did and a second team, which had never seen IBM's code, write new code to match. Phoenix Technologies did the same in 1984 and sold the result to anyone who wanted it. In 1992 the Ninth Circuit ruled in Sega v. Accolade that taking a program apart to learn how it works can be fair use. Copyright protects the code. It does not protect what the code does.
What protected Photoshop all these years was the payroll. Cloning it meant a building full of engineers and several years of their lives, and nobody sane would spend that to give the result away. That bill now fits on a credit card. And if Thomas did decompile something, he broke a license agreement, which makes him a defendant.

| **Math Matters** :** The Cost of Janoo’s ‘Free’ Healthcare Plan **

New reports raise fundamental questions about Amanda Janoo’s promise to deliver “free” universal primary care.

According to an October 8th VTDigger story, **[she doesn’t know how much it will cost or how care will be delivered [1].](https://us.list-manage.com/1CHvCeLQ9RV?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c "https://vtdigger.org/2026/10/08/universal-primary-care-is-at-the-center-of-the-race-for-governor-how-would-it-work/")**

She says she has lots of “estimates.” But never mentions which additional taxes she will raise on Vermonters when the new tax she has identified falls far short.

**_WHAT DOES THE REAL MATH SHOW?_**

A 2016 report from Governor Peter Shumlin’s (D) administration to the Legislature estimated “free” universal primary care would cost between $294.1 million and $316.6 million [2].

Adjusted for Vermont’s medical inflation since 2017, those costs rise to between $580 million and $611 million.

Amanda Janoo’s “wealth tax” – by her own estimates – raises between $114 million and $344 million. _(Side note: She currently proposes to put new income taxes on filers beginning at $250,000 of combined annual income, because she does not believe these households and small businesses pay their “fair share.”)_

**Right out of the gate, her promise starts off $250 million - $500 million in the negative. **

That’s not decimal dust. It would be one of the single largest tax increases in state history.

**Janoo told VTDigger she’s open to “exploring an array of options for funding the program...” _ But never specifies which ones._**

**_WILL IT LOWER COSTS FOR VERMONTERS?_**

Janoo argues that a government-run and taxpayer-funded “free” universal primary care system will save you money by “lowering hospitalizations and reliance on specialty services.”

She describes her savings projections as “a rough estimate intended to gauge whether an ambitious plan for primary care would be feasible and financeable.”

But she never actually shows you the math.

A UVM healthcare policy professor told VTDigger:

**_“I have not seen a lot of evidence that would then lead to markedly fewer expensive specialist visits or emergency room visits.” _**

And:

**_“I am not convinced that this particular idea would have a major return on investment that would justify raising taxes and increasing spending on health care.” _**

**HAVEN’T WE SEEN THIS MOVIE BEFORE?**

Yes. Vermont has been through this exact thing before.

In fact, Vermonters are still paying more, and have fewer choices, because of the same inflexible ideological commitment to an idea that the math – and Democratic party leaders like Governor Peter Shumlin – determined was unworkable at the state level, just 12 years ago.

Voters (and reporters) who were not here for that, or who are under 30, should google:

“Governor Shumlin and Single Payer” for a refresher.

Spoiler alert: Governor Shumlin canceled the plan after years of work because the taxes required were, in his words, “enormous” and the economic consequences too significant.

**WHAT’S GOVERNOR SCOTT’S PLAN?**

Governor Phil Scott wants Vermonters to have universally accessible and affordable healthcare – but has a more affordable, more immediate, and more mainstream plan to get there.

In June, Governor Scott signed Act 173, directing further study on a universal primary care system. When he signed it, he said any universal primary care plan must accomplish critical policy goals:
* Improve access while reducing overall healthcare costs.
* Protect primary care providers, especially in rural communities.
* Strengthen Vermont’s economic growth and economic competitiveness.
* Be something young families and working Vermonters can easily use and truly afford – because no matter what candidates promise on the campaign trail... it won’t be “free.”

The Governor has also, repeatedly, put forward plans to lower healthcare premiums and expand choice – but the supermajority has refused these more affordable, mainstream changes.

His plan uses proven tools – tools virtually every other state is using – available to us through the Affordable Care Act (aka Obamacare) [3].

The same tools allow New Hampshire to offer more plans at a _fraction_ of the cost as Vermont. For example, a family plan can cost Vermonters upwards of $26,000 dollars each year, while in New Hampshire, that same family would pay just $11,000 for the same plan.

If the Legislature passes Governor Scott’s plan, we can protect seniors, increase options, and lower insurance costs for younger workers and families; while restoring affordable options like healthcare co-ops and association plans for small businesses and non-profits.

**Vermonters want real plans and solutions that lower costs NOW. Not another promise of “free” healthcare with no math to pay for it.**

Math matters.

A lot.

_**And with a contribution today, we can continue to shed light on the types of proposals that will cost Vermonters more at a time when we need to do everything we can to make Vermont more affordable, not less.**_ ###

Case File No DRT-ED-SUPPLY · Special File · The New Front Line
Ukraine Didn’t Aim at Tanks. It Burned Russia’s Amazon. Every Business on Earth Just Learned the Lesson.
Since July, Ukrainian drones have hit dozens of warehouses run by Russia’s biggest online retailers. Losses run into the billions, and most of it was uninsured. Modern war goes after supply chains first, and the companies that protect them are moving into the spotlight.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
For most of history, wars were fought over armies, borders and cities. This summer, a new kind of target became the headline: warehouses. Not weapons depots. Regular e-commerce warehouses, full of phones, clothes and household goods.
The evidence board
| | What the Drones Did
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the targets.** The first strikes on Wildberries, which holds about 45% of Russia’s online retail market, came on July 18. Within a month, more than 20 of its warehouses had been hit. In late August, the drones turned to its rival, Ozon.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the damage.** One Russian outlet estimated that about 43% of Wildberries’ warehouse space was lost. Reuters put it at no less than one-fifth. Forbes Russia estimated sellers’ losses at 215 to 280 billion rubles by early August.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the fallout.** About 80% of the buildings and inventory were reportedly uninsured. More than 400,000 sellers were affected. Ozon’s shares fell 27% after a string of strikes in August.
| OUR THEORY
---
Ukraine didn’t need to win a battle to hit Russia’s economy. It went after the systems that move goods. Every company, every army and every government watching has now learned the same lesson: **supply chains are the soft target of modern war.**
Why it matters to you
| | Why This Isn’t Just Russia’s Problem
---|---
| →| **Every Western supply chain is exposed.** Ports, warehouses and distribution hubs are just as hard to protect.
---|---
| →| **Budgets follow fear.** When a threat becomes visible, governments and corporations spend to defend against it, fast.
---|---
| →| **The early solutions win.** Companies that already have proven tools tend to capture the first and largest contracts.
---|---
| ClassificationLesson learned
---
The burning warehouses are on Russia’s side of the border, but the wake-up call is global. Protecting logistics has gone from a back-office issue to a national security priority.
| Open file · unresolvedWho already built the fix?When a new threat suddenly becomes obvious, a few companies are usually years ahead, with solutions designed before anyone else saw the problem. Those are the names that tend to move first once the spending starts.Most investors haven’t connected these dots yet. That may not last.

---
| | | Picture your ballot showing up by certified mail. If you're not home to sign for it, it goes back. According to new reporting from ProPublica, **that's how the Trump White House first wanted mail voting to work.**
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141195081/652754014/-569431239?refcode=261011-mail&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZjYxODk1Ni04Y2M1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=KcIGoyguYOecE2PbxgtlYkypF599k_s_1R_VKWShIgI=)
---
The administration floated a plan to require every ballot to be delivered by certified mail. It was dropped only after the Postal Service warned that it would be impossible to carry out. The plan they ended up with was hardly better. Trump's March executive order would have turned postal workers into gatekeepers, deciding which ballots got delivered and which didn't. It put Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who has no formal authority over the Postal Service, in charge of coordinating it. Postal officials were left out of key conversations, and the order's contents shocked even the Postal Service's own lawyers. **Then the White House insisted that if even one envelope in a batch didn't match a state's voter list, the whole batch should be rejected.** A former postal official told ProPublica what that would mean: **_"If four addresses don't align in a mailing of one million, 999,996 other people don't get their ballot tomorrow."_** Oregon votes entirely by mail. In our state, that would not cause a “glitch” – it would have resulted in our election grinding to a halt. The Supreme Court blocked the order last month. But the reporting makes one thing clear: this was never just a careless mistake. It took nearly a year of planning by people who knew exactly how much disruption they were designing. **They won't stop at one order. As your Secretary of State, I'm going to keep Oregon's vote-by-mail system working for every eligible voter, no matter what the Trump Administration tries next. To do that, I need people standing with me before the next attack comes.** **[Can you chip in $15 to my campaign right now and help us stand up to Trump's attacks on vote-by-mail? ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141195082/652754015/-569431239?refcode=261011-mail&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZjYxODk1Ni04Y2M1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=KcIGoyguYOecE2PbxgtlYkypF599k_s_1R_VKWShIgI=)**

clean_body: | | | = | | | Picture your ballot showing up by certified mail. If you're not home to sign for it, it goes back. According to new reporting from ProPublica, that's how the Trump White House first wanted mail voting to work. = The administration floated a plan to require every ballot to be delivered by certified mail. It was dropped only after the Postal Service warned that it would be impossible to carry out. The plan they ended up with was hardly better. Trump's March executive order would have turned postal workers into gatekeepers, deciding which ballots got delivered and which didn't. It put Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who has no formal authority over the Postal Service, in charge of coordinating it. Postal officials were left out of key conversations, and the order's contents shocked even the Postal Service's own lawyers. Then the White House insisted that if even one envelope in a batch didn't match a state's voter list, the whole batch should be rejected. A former postal official told ProPublica what that would mean: "If four addresses don't align in a mailing of one million, 999,996 other people don't get their ballot tomorrow." Oregon votes entirely by mail. In our state, that would not cause a “glitch” – it would have resulted in our election grinding to a halt. The Supreme Court blocked the order last month. But the reporting makes one thing clear: this was never just a careless mistake. It took nearly a year of planning by people who knew exactly how much disruption they were designing. They won't stop at one order. As your Secretary of State, I'm going to keep Oregon's vote-by-mail system working for every eligible voter, no matter what the Trump Administration tries next. To do that, I need people standing with me before the next attack comes. = = Thank you for having Oregon's back, Tobias ReadOregon Secretary of State | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Friends of Tobias Read (5208) PO Box 42307 Portland, OR 97242 United States If you believe you received this message in error or wish to no longer receive email from us, please .

I refuse to sit by while people continue to lose access to critical programs.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3976%2E21716%2ELMGQhR)
**Last month, the Trump administration canceled Affordable Care Act Marketplace coverage for more than 750,000 Americans.**
They’ve claimed the cancellations are based on fraud or ineligibility, but they’ve provided _zero_ evidence to prove it.
Over 19 million Americans rely on coverage from the Affordable Care Act, with the cost of living — and specifically healthcare costs — continuously increasing across the country.
And for the last two years, Donald Trump and Republicans in Congress have been continually cutting the programs working families rely on so they can give tax breaks to their billionaire friends.
**We even saw DOGE ransack the government while leaving real cases of fraud untouched.** All while neglecting to implement alternatives, leaving the costs of these cuts to fall on the backs of hardworking Americans.
I want to be clear: We absolutely have a duty to deliver accountability and root out waste, fraud, and abuse. But we need to do it without denying our neighbors access to the critical lifelines they desperately need.
In order to keep Delaware’s seat in Congress blue, bring true accountability to this administration, and make sure everyone who needs it has access to crucial programs like the Affordable Care Act, we need to make sure we’re reaching Delawareans up and down the state.

A man in his sixties. A paraplegic, in a wheelchair. Lined up in front of members of the United States military so they can shoot him. And maybe livestreamed on the fucking internet, or carried live on Fox News.
That's what Pete Hegseth wants. He just announced that America will carry out its first public execution in nearly 100 years.
I haven't been able to shake it. I shot a video on it. I talked about it on CNN Friday night. And this weekend, at a family wedding, surrounded by people I love, I kept coming back to it. How did we get here? What the hell are we doing?
I do not want to live in a country that carries out public executions. That puts us on the same list as Iran, North Korea and Afghanistan, and I can't think of many lists I'd want to share with those three.
Let me be clear: the man they plan to put to death is a monster. What he did was horrific, and I have no sympathy for him. But I don't believe in the death penalty. I think it's morally wrong, and it's a terrible deterrent. The idea that someone set on a murderous rampage will stop to weigh the consequences has always seemed silly to me. And turning it into a public spectacle doesn't make it justice. It makes it theater.
We've always known there's cruelty and chaos at the heart of Donald Trump and the MAGA movement. We see it in what they say. We see it in what they do. We see it in who they use the government to help and who they use it to hurt.
But even this seems to be too much for a lot of them. J.D. Vance, the Vice President of the United States, was asked about it and looked deeply uncomfortable. Even Trump seemed a little unnerved.
Pete Hegseth, though? That slobbering, disgusting, incompetent boob is thrilled.
I'm convinced very few Americans actually want this. Outside a handful of dipshit incels who worship guys like Hegseth and the Tate brothers, there's no audience for it. So why are we pandering to those losers? Why are we tolerating this?
Here's the thing: the votes to remove Pete Hegseth exist right now. Republicans and Democrats are sick of his bullshit. And Mike Johnson shut down Congress to protect him.
This guy has got to go. He's dumb. He's corrupt. He's destroying our military. He's purging hardworking people. And he's doing stupid shit like this that sets America back and makes us look horrible on the world stage.
I have a ton of empathy for everyone, including people who didn't vote for the candidates I believe in. But if you can hear the news of a public execution and your heart doesn't sink, something is fundamentally wrong in your soul.
So here's my optimistic note: we don't have to tolerate this shit anymore. We have these guys on the run. When Democrats take back the House and the Senate in November, we'll have the power to remove Pete Hegseth ourselves.
Most of this fight will be about the economy. It'll be about the corruption and the lives they've wrecked. But it's also about who we are. And I keep thinking about that wedding. A room full of people dancing, crying, laughing, holding each other. That's America. That's the country worth fighting for. Not a firing squad on a livestream.

subject: Trump’s secret AI “regulation” plan: Written by Zuck and Musk
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
I’m demanding answers from Trump’s White House

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3051%2E4032634%2EAqxhSe)
---
Imagine if the tobacco companies got to decide which cigarettes the FDA was allowed to inspect. Or if Wall Street firms could tell the SEC which trades it could investigate. You’d call that a pretty obvious conflict of interest. Right? So why are we letting the biggest AI companies in the world help decide how they should be regulated? AI is moving too fast for the government to simply hope Big Tech will do the right thing. So the Trump administration, at first, was developing a process to test powerful AI systems for serious security risks. It was kind of a no-brainer if you ask me: before these systems are widely deployed, experts should have a chance to find out whether they could be used to attack our banks, power grid, hospitals, or other critical infrastructure. Then the CEOs got involved. Executives from Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic reportedly objected to parts of the process. And Trump’s buddies Mark Zuckerberg and Elon Musk also raised concerns. And the rules changed. What had been considered a “requirement” is now more of a suggestion. The review process was shortened, and the details still being worked out are being handled behind closed doors. The American people have no oversight or say. The companies that are supposed to be regulated are getting a say in the rules meant to regulate them. And I, for one, am not going to sit back and watch it happen. I’m demanding that the top officials in Trump’s White House release every communication between these companies and the administration about the AI policy. We need to know about their secret AI framework and how it impacts the public. The American people deserve strong guardrails set by democratically elected officials, not a toothless framework shaped in secret by a handful of billionaires. I’m going to keep pushing until we know what happened and the American people can see how these decisions are being made. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth Warren | **Elizabeth Warren has called for an immediate pause on advanced AI development so that Congress can put proper guardrails and regulations in place to prevent serious harm. She has also introduced policies to tax AI companies to prevent an economic collapse, and to make AI companies pay for their own data center usage that is jacking up utility prices.** **If you’re able, pitch in to power this work.** | [**DONATE NOW**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3841?t=8&akid=3051%2E4032634%2EAqxhSe)

I want to be very transparent with you.

I am National Republicans' top target. They're coming after me with everything they’ve got.

Over the past few weeks, billionaire donors like Elon Musk, tech scion Peter Thiel, and dark-money groups have dumped millions into Ohio to crush our momentum – because if we lose here, we’ll lose our shot at taking back the Senate and breaking Republicans’ grip on power.

Total GOP spending in this race has now reached _over $270 million._

I know I ask a lot of this team, but I hope you know I wouldn’t be reaching out if it weren’t so important. And right now, it is: We just missed our daily fundraising goal, and we have just over 72 hours until the final FEC deadline of this election – when we’ll have to report our fundraising numbers for everyone to see.

This is our wake up call to step it up.

**The only way we can get back on track is with a massive surge of grassroots support from folks like you, so I need to try something different today. I’m lowering my ask to just $1 in the hopes that every person reading this chips in so we can build back our momentum.**

Senator presses Hegseth, Caine for commitment to keep US military out of the midterm elections
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2517%2E135344%2EXa_WJr)

Earlier this year, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth came before the Senate Armed Services Committee to answer questions about the war in Iran, the defense budget, and other matters.
Among other questions, I asked this one:
Will you deploy the uniformed military to the polls to collect voter rolls or machines in the upcoming election?
He wouldn't answer.
There is no shortage of issues out there, but this one is fundamental: the uniformed military shouldn't be deployed to interfere in our elections. Period. It taints our democracy. It taints our military. And it would set both down a course that may be hard to ever come back from.
Please read this article from the Associated Press and share it with friends.
* * *
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-26.79HKre&refcode=em261010&t=2&akid=2517%2E135344%2EXa_WJr)
**Senator presses Hegseth, Caine for commitment to keep US military out of the midterm elections**
WASHINGTON (AP) — Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin asked Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday to confirm he won’t send U.S. troops to polling places during November’s midterm elections, as Democrats have raised concerns that the Trump administration could use the military to interfere with the vote.
“I’d ask you to confirm a simple statement: the Department of Defense will not send Federal troops to the polls or to seize election materials of any kind,” Slotkin wrote to Hegseth and to Gen. Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, in letters Tuesday.
The Pentagon said in an email that it will respond directly to Slotkin, as it does with all congressional correspondence. The Joint Chiefs did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Slotkin told The Associated Press that Trump has been laying the groundwork to claim the midterms were stolen. She noted that Trump contemplated using the military to seize voting machines after his loss in 2020 and has deployed the National Guard to cities against the wishes of Democratic leaders. He also deployed active duty Marines to Los Angeles during his immigration crackdown in 2025.
“He’s very clearly laying the breadcrumbs to be able to say the day after the election that he didn’t really lose the House or he didn’t really lose the Senate,” Slotkin said.
Slotkin asked Hegseth during an April congressional hearing if he would follow orders to seize ballots. Hegseth called the question a “gotcha hypothetical,” but said, “I’ve never been ordered to do anything illegal, and I won’t.”
White House chief of staff Susie Wiles denied in a Vanity Fair interview last year that Trump would use the military to suppress voting in the midterms.
“I say it is categorically false, will not happen. It’s just wrongheaded,” she said.
Federal law prohibits the deployment of armed federal forces to election locations unless “necessary to repel armed enemies of the United States.” If any element of the military were to get involved, it would likely be the National Guard under state control.
In 2020, Gen. Mark Milley, then-chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, responded to a similar letter from Slotkin, then a congresswoman.
“I believe deeply in the principle of an apolitical U.S. military,” Milley wrote. “In the event of a dispute over some aspect of the elections, by law U.S. courts and the U.S. Congress are required to resolve any disputes, not the U.S. military.”

* * *

As one of the few Senators who won a Senate race in the same state won by Trump, Elissa Slotkin is being asked to campaign for other Democrats in tough races across the country this election.
And while Elissa wishes we did not have to send another email asking you to contribute, that is what we have to do today.

Dear Fellow Patriot:

The gun grabbers just put a price tag on your Second Amendment rights.

**Ten million dollars.**

That’s what the Giffords gun control machine announced it will spend between now and Election Day, smearing pro-Second Amendment candidates and peddling anti-gun propaganda.

And the timing couldn’t be worse for gun owners.

As I write you, anti-gun Democrats hold an 8-point lead in the RealClearPolitics generic ballot. **That’s even bigger than their lead in the final 2018 polls, the year Democrats flipped 41 seats.**

The U.S. Senate doesn’t look any better. Polymarket – the major prediction market where people put real money on the line – shows gun grabbers poised to flip five seats and seize control of the U.S. Senate.

The national media is ready to pile on and proclaim voters handed anti-gun Democrats a “mandate” to RAM through gun control the moment the new Congress is sworn in.

**And even if they fall short next year, they’ll have set the stage for a President Gavin Newsom or Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez in 2028!**

My name is Dudley Brown. I’m the President of the National Association for Gun Rights, America’s no-compromise gun lobby. I’ve spent the better part of my life fighting these people, and I can tell you they don’t spend money like this because they’re winning the argument.

They spend it to buy seats, so their pet politicians are in place and ready to pounce.

I’m not about to let that happen without a fight. And I’m betting you won’t either.

[Will you please agree to your most generous contribution to help the National Association for Gun Rights EXPOSE the gun grabbers before it’s too late](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**?**

As you’ll see below, I’ve laid out exactly what your support for the National Association for Gun Rights will do today.
[>>> YES, I’LL FIGHT BACK AGAINST GIFFORDS’ $10 MILLION <<<](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
This isn’t the first time Giffords has tried to buy Congress.

In 2022, they announced a $10 million spending spree. In 2024, they upped it to $15 million. Now they’re back with another $10 million, and they’re hinting there’s more on the way.

That’s at least $35 million in three election cycles. And every time, they’ve told us exactly what they want for their money.

We know because the last time anti-gun Democrats held the House, they voted for: *** **A sweeping “Assault Weapons” ban, outlawing many of America’s most popular rifles.** It passed the House in 2022.

*** **So-called “universal” background checks, the first step toward a national gun registry.** It passed the House in 2019 and again in 2021.

*** **A federal “Red Flag” law, letting courts strip your firearms without you ever being charged with a crime.** It passed the House in 2022. The only thing that stopped these bills was the U.S. Senate filibuster.

That’s why they’re gunning for the Senate now. And once they control it, they’ve promised to finish the job: >>> **Nuke the filibuster** so they can pass gun control with a bare majority.

>>> **Pack the Supreme Court** with anti-gun Justices to overturn Heller and Bruen, the landmark rulings protecting your right to keep and bear arms.

>>> **Grant statehood to Washington, D.C. and Puerto Rico** , giving themselves four new Senate seats and a lock on power for a generation. If they pull this off, they won’t just pass gun control. They’ll rig the system so it can never be undone.

[Help the National Association for Gun Rights Expose the Gun Grabbers >>](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

With your support, the National Association for Gun Rights is launching an all-out, final-stretch campaign in the key races that will decide who controls the U.S. Senate.

Our goal is simple. We’re going to ensure pro-Second Amendment patriots know where their politicians stand in these states with: **1\. Hard-hitting targeted TV ads.** Our ads are already made and ready to run in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, North Carolina, Alaska, Georgia, Michigan, New Hampshire, and Minnesota.

Each one exposes a gun grabber’s anti-Second Amendment record in plain English. And with our technology, we’ll be able to target the exact households we’ve identified as low propensity, pro-gun voters to ensure they get out to the polls.

**2\. Direct mail into pro-gun households.** We’ll put the candidates’ records on paper and into the mailboxes of pro-gun households in these states. A commercial is over in thirty seconds. A letter is a physical reminder that can’t be ignored.

**3\. Email and social media blasts.** Gun owners in every target state will get the facts, with the voting records and the paper trail to back them up, delivered straight to their inboxes and news feeds.

**4\. Targeted online ads.** Digital ads on social media and the websites gun owners visit every day mean the truth follows them from the TV to their phone and back again. [Help the National Association for Gun Rights Expose the Gun Grabbers >>](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

I know this works because we did it in Pennsylvania in 2024.

Senator Bob Casey had held that seat for nearly two decades.

His family had been a political dynasty in Pennsylvania since the Kennedy years.

He spent his whole career passing himself off as a friend of gun owners while voting for red flag gun confiscation and the biggest expansion of gun registration in decades.

He led in the early polls. He had a 2-to-1 fundraising advantage. The so-called “experts” all but crowned him.

So we went to work. We identified 88,000 pro-gun households across Pennsylvania and hit them with mail, email after email, and hard-hitting TV ads exposing Casey’s anti-gun record.

On Election Night, Bob Casey lost by one-fifth of one percent.

**One-fifth of one percent.**

That’s the kind of margin gun owners who know the truth can make.

But this year, the fight isn’t one state. It’s nine.

And thanks to streaming TV technology, your gift goes further than ever before. *** $26 puts our ads exposing the gun grabbers in front of 354 pro-gun households.
*** $50 reaches 681 households.
*** $100 reaches 1,362 households.
*** $250 reaches 3,405 households.
*** $500 reaches 6,810 households. Think about that. A single $50 gift reaches a whole neighborhood of gun owners. **Every one of them will know exactly where their Senate candidate stands before they cast a ballot.**

Giffords has $10 million. We have you.

And every day we wait is a day their ads run unanswered. Once ballots are cast, no ad in the world can change the outcome.

[Will you chip in $26 right now to put our ads in front of 354 pro-gun households](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**?**
[>>> YES, I’LL PUT OUR ADS IN FRONT OF 354 PRO-GUN HOUSEHOLDS <<<](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
If you can, please give $50 or even $100. That puts the truth in front of 681 or 1,362 households before Election Day.

For Freedom,

**Dudley Brown
President
National Association for Gun Rights**

P.S. Giffords just committed $10 million to buy the seats that decide control of the U.S. Senate. NAGR’s TV ads exposing the gun grabbers’ records are ready to run to targeted households during football games in the key Senate states right up to Election Day.

Every $26 you give puts our ads in front of 354 pro-gun households. [Please make your most generous possible gift right now to keep them on the air](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.).

subject: I rock my ribbon skirt to honor my ancestors
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/1102?refcode=jtk1537-fr-nd&t=1&akid=13033%2E400544%2Et8mOSG)
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17482?refcode=jtk1537-fr-nd&t=2&akid=13033%2E400544%2Et8mOSG)
Hi friend, it's Deb Haaland. I am the daughter of Pueblo women, a single mother, a former small business owner, a former Congresswoman, and the first Native American Cabinet Secretary in U.S. history. **And thanks to your support, I am the official Democratic nominee for Governor of New Mexico.**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17482?refcode=jtk1537-fr-nd&t=3&akid=13033%2E400544%2Et8mOSG)
---
But no matter where I go and no matter what role I serve in, **I'm a proud Pueblo woman.** That's why I often wear my mocs or my ribbon skirt. These symbols remind me of how powerful traditional clothing is in sharing our heritage, and they remind me to honor the shoulders I stand on.

In a minute, I'm going to share some of the places I've rocked my ribbon skirt and mocs. [ _**But before I do, I have to ask:**_**_Will you please help fuel our fight to the general election by giving $5 to my campaign right now?_**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17603?refcode=jtk1537-fr-nd&t=4&akid=13033%2E400544%2Et8mOSG)
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17482?refcode=jtk1537-fr-nd&t=5&akid=13033%2E400544%2Et8mOSG)
---
| | On the day I was sworn in as Secretary of the Interior, I decided to wear my white moccasins and a handmade ribbon skirt adorned with butterflies, stars, and corn. No matter where I go, I am a proud Pueblo woman first — including at the Department of the Interior.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/8175?refcode=jtk1537-fr-nd&t=6&akid=13033%2E400544%2Et8mOSG)
---
| | On the first day of the White House Tribal Nations Summit in 2021, I wore my beaded moccasins in solidarity with our Indigenous people across the country. I am incredibly grateful that together, our administration made extraordinary accomplishments for Indian Country — enduring progress that would make our ancestors proud.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17482?refcode=jtk1537-fr-nd&t=7&akid=13033%2E400544%2Et8mOSG)
---
| | From my ancestral homelands here in New Mexico to the halls of Congress — and as I filed my candidate petition to add my name to New Mexico's ballot for Governor — I rock my ribbon skirt to honor my ancestors.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17482?refcode=jtk1537-fr-nd&t=8&akid=13033%2E400544%2Et8mOSG)
---
Friend, history has shown us there's nothing we can't accomplish when we work together, which is why I'm counting on the support of people like you as we fight for a New Mexico that works for everyone.
And with less than four weeks to go until Election Day, we are one step closer to making this vision a reality.

**_[Please, friend: Will you chip in $5 right now so we can build a strong campaign capable of winning this race and making history again?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17603?refcode=jtk1537-fr-nd&t=9&akid=13033%2E400544%2Et8mOSG)_**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17482?refcode=jtk1537-fr-nd&t=10&akid=13033%2E400544%2Et8mOSG)
---
I am so grateful for your support. Thank you for being by my side.

Be fierce,
Deb

Friends,
Election Day is just 23 days away, and the stakes could not be higher. What happens this fall will decide the future of Wisconsin and who controls Congress.Here at home, every race on the ballot matters, from the Governor’s office to the State Legislature. In Washington, the House majority is on the line, and Democrats are pouring money into the fight to take it back. If they win, they will stop the work we’ve done to secure the border, cut wasteful spending, and keep more money in Wisconsin families’ pockets.That’s why I’m not taking a single vote for granted. A big turnout helps Republicans up and down the ballot here in Wisconsin and helps protect our majority in the House. Not anyone.| | | | Peter, I've been on the road for the last month, campaigning for Democrats who will help take back control of the House and Senate. One issue keeps coming up: the Epstein class. People are tired of watching the wealthy and powerful play by one set of rules while everyone else lives by another. I have been to Iowa for Josh Turek, to New Hampshire for Chris Pappas, and going to Nebraska for Dan Osborn. I have campaigned for Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and Randy Villegas in California. I plan to spend the next 20 days on the road. = = We must call out a two-tier justice system where the elite use wealth and influence to escape scrutiny and accountability. From New Hampshire to Iowa to Nebraska to California, Americans are ready to vote for leaders who will stand up to concentrated power and demand the truth. ---

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bccce985-f142-4dbe-b10e-703e2fbf286b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The frozen pizza business is booming...and that's concerning. That probably sounds strange. But not if you understand what frozen pizza actually _is,_ economically speaking. Frozen pizza isn't a product. It's a _signal_. And right now, the signal is flashing red.
You see, frozen pizza thrives when the economy doesn't. In 2009, at the depths of the Great Recession, frozen pizza sales surged while restaurants sat empty. When COVID hit in 2020, [sales jumped roughly a billion dollars in a single year](https://substack.com/redirect/3d9a8aac-795d-401b-8037-61ce7488c55f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), from $5.6 billion to $6.6 billion. The pattern is proving so reliable, it's almost mechanical: when families start trading down from dining out to eating in, that journey includes regular stops in the frozen food aisle.
And right now? The frozen aisle is as busy as ever.
* * *
## [The Fed Needs to Consume More Pizza (Data)](https://substack.com/redirect/b44fd58f-6f88-4567-94ec-d3ecfd3831d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Vikram Mansharamani](https://substack.com/profile/37278065-vikram-mansharamani)| | *
---|---|---
| Apr 26
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b44fd58f-6f88-4567-94ec-d3ecfd3831d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[I have a weakness for seemingly irrelevant indicators. Nearly fifteen years ago, I wrote in Forbes that the race to build the world's tallest skyscraper was a more robust indicator of forthcoming chaos than most traditional measures that economists track](https://substack.com/redirect/b44fd58f-6f88-4567-94ec-d3ecfd3831d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/b44fd58f-6f88-4567-94ec-d3ecfd3831d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
U.S. frozen pizza sales hit [nearly $7 billion in 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/3d9a8aac-795d-401b-8037-61ce7488c55f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), part of a broader frozen food category that just crossed [$87 billion annually](https://substack.com/redirect/21092644-fbef-44f2-873e-d8c2d5aacd88?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), up dramatically since 2019. But lest you think it's just inflation driving the numbers, think again. Unit volume is up almost 5%. People aren't just paying more for the same stuff; they're buying _more_ stuff.
The foot traffic data tells a similar story. Year-over-year gains at value-focused grocery stores while pizza chain visits have gone sideways. Consumers are shifting from eating out to takeout and then on to frozen food at home as a cost-saving measure. [Forty percent](https://substack.com/redirect/5a10ce8d-f7b3-4e90-b123-b09eceea8e51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of consumers now say they reach for frozen foods daily, up from 35% in 2019. Nearly a third say they plan to buy even more in the year ahead, citing difficult economic circumstances.
* * *
## [Pizza Power and The Economy](https://substack.com/redirect/9de83791-a03e-4da7-bf44-1cccd28796ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Vikram Mansharamani](https://substack.com/profile/37278065-vikram-mansharamani)| | *
---|---|---
| December 15, 2025
[](https://substack.com/redirect/9de83791-a03e-4da7-bf44-1cccd28796ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Earlier this year, I wrote a short piece about pizza's power to predict major domestic and geopolitical events, noting that unusually large late night pizza order delivered to the Pentagon, White House, or even Congress had been correlated with major geopolitical developments emerging from Washington DC. After all, during an emerging or ongoing crisis, ...](https://substack.com/redirect/9de83791-a03e-4da7-bf44-1cccd28796ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/9de83791-a03e-4da7-bf44-1cccd28796ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
I recently wrote about the "trench coat economy," the idea that headline GDP growth is masking deep fragility in the broad economy. The frozen food aisle is Exhibit A. Official numbers say we're in an expansion. The [Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index](https://substack.com/redirect/aeeb35aa-a840-4ab8-b22d-2c6b3198db46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) says otherwise; it recently posted the lowest reading since May 2020. When consumers tell surveyors they're pessimistic and then back it up by loading their carts with frozen pizza, that's not anecdotal evidence. That's hard data.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/682df857-9fbf-4617-8240-0e782b385ab5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Here's what I see from my perspective running a frozen pizza factory that serves major American retailers through private label offerings. Private label is a key driver of growth in the category, and we're the _last_ stop on the trade-down escalator. Consumers don't switch from restaurants to private-label frozen pizza in one step. First, they cut back on fine dining. Then they downshift to fast casual. Then on to fast food. Then name-brand frozen. Then, when things get really stressed and budgets tighten even further, consumers reach for store brands.
* * *
## [Pizza's Power to Predict](https://substack.com/redirect/f1ef2ded-0053-4445-874b-4808ccc731b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---

* * *
Every week's private label point-of-sale data is a story of families across America making trade-offs. More demand is a signal that more people are tightening their belts. If you look in the right spot, you can see consumer stress before it shows up in the confidence data.
Economists love their leading indicators: yield curves, purchasing manager surveys, housing starts. I'd like to suggest they add one more: year over year frozen pizza sales. And if they want to get more specific, private label pizza sales. When the store brands start flying off the shelves, something is happening that the GDP print isn't catching. The disconnect between the macroeconomic statistics and the reality faced by most Americans is growing, and it points to a rapidly slowing economy.
So if you want to get a sense of where the economy is heading, look at the shopping carts of American families as they leave the supermarket.

subject: Early voting starting in North Carolina
body:
We’re down to the wire, Peter.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1643&source=&t=1&akid=4405%2E124072%2EBBmCP8) | | | | Peter,
---
Early voting starts this Thursday in North Carolina and I’m feeling hopeful.
I know you’re getting a lot of messages right now, so thank you for opening my email and staying engaged. I appreciate it.
Here’s the thing: Our final FEC deadline of the election is Wednesday at midnight, and right now, we’re falling short of our $3 million goal. This is the last time our numbers will go public before Election Day, which means it’s our last chance to show the strength of our grassroots movement.
If we come up short, not only will we have to scale back our get-out-the-vote efforts, but we’ll also send a message to Michael Whatley and his MAGA allies that we don’t have what it takes to win this – and they’ll pounce.
Peter, we can’t let that happen.
**It doesn’t look like you’ve chipped in to our campaign yet. I understand – but today, I’m hoping that changes.** With early voting starting in just a few days – and the final FEC deadline of the race on Wednesday – we can’t afford to come up short.

**The only way we can fight back against the GOP’s attacks and make sure our supporters turn out to vote is if new donors like you join me at this crucial moment.**
[**_$5 is the most strategic donation you can make right now to help us keep our momentum, flip the Senate for Democrats and return power to the people.
