Somewhere in Bengaluru this morning, a curriculum producer is drafting a reading lesson for a seventh-grader in Texas. The lesson covers the Texas Revolution -- the Alamo, San Jacinto, annexation. The producer has probably never set foot in Texas. The seventh-grader will never know the difference.
The producer's employer is paid by that seventh-grader's school district. Which means, if you're a Texas taxpayer, you're the one cutting the check.
**The company**
Imagine Learning, headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, was founded by Jonathan Grayer as a partnership with KKR and has grown -- by its own account -- into the largest digital curriculum provider to K-12 schools in the U.S., serving over 18 million students in over half of the districts nationwide. Those aren't my numbers; they're the company's. This is not a bit player skirting the edge of the classroom. This is the spine of American K-12 content.
And the spine is being built out, in considerable part, offshore.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5ce039c5-a7f3-434e-92e6-0b5a3ac2afbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The buildout**
Imagine Learning's own India careers page says it plainly: "World class work. Real impact. Right here in Bengaluru." Engineers, data scientists and product innovators there, the site says, work "to shape how millions of students and educators experience learning -- everyday." Indian business press reports the Bengaluru center has hired roughly 85 people, headed for 100 by the end of 2026, with a heavy emphasis on AI and engineering.
The viral investigation that blew this open surfaced job postings from the company's India operation for curriculum architects, instructional designers and English language arts managers -- people in Bengaluru developing American K-12 reading lessons, writing assignments, literature questions, essay prompts and assessments aligned with U.S. state education standards -- and for managers to oversee curriculum decisions and AI-assisted lesson development.
It doesn't stop at one office. Infosys -- the outsourcing giant that taught three generations of Americans to press one for English -- says on its own channels that it has stood up two AI-first global capability centers for Imagine Learning, in Chandigarh and Pune, serving product engineering, business systems and operations. The Straive-LearningMate group, whose global operations center sits in India and whose service list reads like a curriculum factory -- learning design, curriculum development, AI ops, content transformation -- has been described as an Imagine Learning partner of more than a decade's standing. Even the Karnataka government has publicly promoted the operation, AI, data science and all.
Notice the phrase "AI-first." That's the tell. This isn't just offshore workers writing lessons. It's offshore teams supervising the artificial intelligence that will write the next generation of lessons. Whatever the machine absorbs now -- our standards, our reading lists, our framing of the Alamo -- it repeats forever. That is a sovereign asset being fed into a grinder, one work order at a time.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/93c91f46-cd11-4657-bd5a-a796d49c3719?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The Texas link**
Now follow the money home. The investigation identified more than $7.7 million in Texas district contracts, purchasing authorizations and payment records. And look at what Imagine Learning markets to Texas schools: seventh-grade Texas history. Eighth-grade U.S. history. U.S. history since 1877. American government. English language arts. A Houston charter school's grant application to the Texas Education Agency specifically named Imagine Learning for seventh-grade Texas history and eighth- and eleventh-grade U.S. history.
That's not software support. That's the San Jacinto lesson. Somebody writes those lessons. Somebody decides which heroes, which compromises, which villains, which words go in the essay prompt. For forty years American parents have fought ferociously over what's in the curriculum -- school boards, standards committees, book shelves, culture wars. It turns out we were arguing over the menu while the kitchen moved to another country.
The question Texas parents should ask is not whether a lesson leans left or right. It's whether it was written in this country at all, and who holds final editorial authority. No one at the Texas Education Agency has answered that on the record.
**The data**
Then there's the part that should worry every parent regardless of politics. Imagine Learning's own privacy policy says its platforms can collect student names, assessment results, writing samples, audio recordings, demographic information, and sensitive indicators -- IEP status, foster care, homelessness. The company says personal information is stored and processed in the United States. It is also hiring platform and data engineers in India.
Both things can be true. Neither answers the question that matters: Can employees or contractors overseas remotely access identifiable student records? Do Infosys or LearningMate personnel touch them? What exactly do the Texas contracts permit? FERPA was written in 1974 for a world of filing cabinets and mimeograph machines. The audit has never been done.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e0e9d7d0-e0c7-44c6-bbb6-50603d44bc9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
# Infosys ECC Campus - Pune, Maharashtra
**We 've been here before**
We've heard "it's just the periphery" before. We outsourced the factory and were told we'd keep the design. We outsourced the call center and were told we'd keep the customer. We outsourced radiology reads, tax preparation, animation, chip design, legal document review -- each time reassured it was back office, overhead, nothing essential. And each time, nothing essential crept inward until it reached the one thing schools actually produce: the content of children's minds.
Texans got a preview this year when headlines revealed districts importing English teachers from India. That was the warm-up. Teachers can be hired. Curriculum, once the authorship migrates, is far harder to bring home.
To be clear where this argument should not go: none of this is a knock on the engineers and content producers of Bengaluru. They are doing exactly what the market asked of them, well. The blame belongs to a Scottsdale boardroom that decided American curriculum was a line item to arbitrage, and to procurement officers in Austin and a hundred other statehouses who never asked the question -- because the vendor's name sounds like a sunrise and the contracts arrive with a state seal on them.
**What should happen**
The fix is not isolationism. It is rudimentary self-government, and it fits on an index card:
1\. A full audit of Imagine Learning in Texas -- every taxpayer dollar, every offshore contractor, every curriculum author, every AI workflow, every permission to access student data.
2\. A procurement rule, this session: any instructional material bought with state money must disclose where it was developed, by whom, and who may access student records. No offshore access to identifiable student data. Period.
3\. A domestic-authorship preference for core academic content, the way we treat defense procurement. Texas already proved a state can build its own curriculum in-house.
4\. A parents' right to know: if lessons were written 9,000 miles away, the district says so on its website.
**The point**
How many of you knew? That's the whole problem. Nobody told you, because for thirty years the outsourcing of America has been executed between board meetings and procurement cycles -- always justified, never announced.
We were told sovereignty is a nostalgic illusion, that a country which no longer makes things can still be great. But a country that no longer writes its own lessons is not a country with a skills gap. It is a country with a succession plan drafted by strangers.
Texas declared independence because people here believed they were the best judges of their own children's future -- and settled it in six weeks at San Jacinto. The least we owe those kids is the sentence explaining why.

_Ninety seconds..._ **That's about how long an ICE arrest takes now, from the moment agents show up to the moment someone is gone, according to one immigration attorney who spoke to The Guardian.** One man in Miami was taken outside his home after he stepped out to take out the trash. A father in Connecticut was arrested after he walked his son to the school bus. _ICE has traded the big, televised raids that sparked public outrage for quick, quiet arrests like these._ And it's arresting more people than ever. August set a new record, the third month in a row. **Once people with final deportation orders are inside, they don't appear in ICE's public locator at all, so their lawyers and families can't find them.** [**We’re fighting back. Will you split a $10, $20, or even $100 contribution between OnePA and The Workers Circle to support the Freedom Advocates program and file three habeas petitions?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqu-wUwIZ511oDywi-RcGpMm0-1_75ztOiSo5PpJdSF8Z5Kb-6fs30gmYH5gI0YIbNCH10LEeNJ8Yzquiqj6ZsOIMjkIVv-mb7aIQLfsHiTW48HO5KWGr1qK8Nns2LhAr6rCRYWNX8IFJxxWrsGOsnW6oyMQVKYYDDVGF8uHVI8sGMd-_sFiHA-htieREKHoG4WZcbGFoTyXlmmfnaNBVd5QS2D30ayBmW8EEM_EA7lTQqi0P5jw1_uUHYfR8VDllWPrxCL7X5dfG1R_eqQzeSkcHb6Pfc1HDwTC0YMcfz6iTt391mz1ANPxuAuJmDIIfTg0bmEADctH0n4Jy45Ph8QaIDStskjVcKSReC8gYm9ouGiTpXAAyTDiWpT5Rx7MSGU/4us/czN4DTVpRJG4HwAW0h0GbA/h1/h001.HTMjZ5VOs5MCaUtitDCVHbZpvecMTbQaftX53t6Odjo)**These petitions help prevent people from disappearing,****Peter****** It's much harder to disappear someone who has legal representation. clean_body: | | Peter, did you see this? Ninety seconds... That's about how long an ICE arrest takes now, from the moment agents show up to the moment someone is gone, according to one immigration attorney who spoke to The Guardian. One man in Miami was taken outside his home after he stepped out to take out the trash. A father in Connecticut was arrested after he walked his son to the school bus. ICE has traded the big, televised raids that sparked public outrage for quick, quiet arrests like these. And it's arresting more people than ever. August set a new record, the third month in a row. Once people with final deportation orders are inside, they don't appear in ICE's public locator at all, so their lawyers and families can't find them. petitions help prevent people from disappearing,Peter** It's much harder to disappear someone who has legal representation. An attorney knows where they are and can file a habeas petition, which forces the government to justify, in front of a federal judge, why it's holding them. While the case is heard, the attorney can ask the court to stop the deportation. The Workers Circle and OnePA are trying to raise $15,000 by the end of this weekend to put Freedom Advocates low-cost attorneys on all three cases. ICE is counting on moving faster than anyone can help. Abbott has failed all of Texas’s 254 counties.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Texas is a big state. **In fact, Texas has more counties than any other state in the country.**
With **254 counties,** from the Panhandle to the Rio Grande Valley, East Texas to the Hill Country, every community has its own story, its own challenges, and its own vision for the future.
But too many Texans have been left behind by Greg Abbott’s leadership.
**[We’ve got more to say, but first, can you pitch in $2.54 — a penny for each of the 254 counties Abbott has failed?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261011_2_254.CGrIp5&refcode=em20261011-2383&amount=2.54&t=1&akid=2383%2E299639%2EyMLYth)**

Gina has traveled thousands of miles across Texas, sitting down with voters, listening to their concerns, and hearing what they need from their next governor.
She’s met teachers worried about the future of public education. Families struggling with rising costs. Small business owners trying to keep their doors open. Rural communities fighting to have a say in decisions that impact their land, resources, and way of life.
And everywhere she goes, Gina hears the same message: **Texans are ready for leadership that actually shows up.**
Greg Abbott has spent years prioritizing billionaire donors, corporate interests, and political insiders. But this campaign is about something different.
We’re building a Texas where every community has a voice and every family has a chance to thrive.
That’s why we’re building this campaign the grassroots way — one conversation, one supporter, and one county at a time.

DELHI, India--Indian authorities enforced an unprecedented crackdown on demonstrations across Delhi on Saturday and Sunday, as student groups and citizen networks, including lawyers and doctors organized to provide support for people protesting a massive purge of voter lists. The government deployed over 20,000 police and paramilitary personnel to prevent protestors from gathering in the city, pulling forces from border areas, including Kashmir, into Delhi.
For the past two weeks, protestors across India have been demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, after an investigation by The Indian Express,__ a prominent daily, revealed that the country's election commission had deleted more than 130 million people from voter rolls without due process.
The call for large demonstrations on Saturday was made by the [Cockroach Janata Party](https://substack.com/redirect/f14bb1fd-ee9e-4ddf-bb80-d8b9508797da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (CJP), which in July led widespread protests against the education minister Dharmendra Pradhan for irregularities in nationwide examinations, leading to his resignation. On Saturday, Delhi police detained Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of CJP, along with several other leaders of the group, on their airplane when they arrived at the Delhi airport, holding them until Sunday morning.
The mobilization was supposed to be held at the designated protest site of Jantar Mantar, but it was entirely barricaded by the police, and most of central Delhi was under police lockdown.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8ea68d71-9201-4107-ac0e-c207ea1df9a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Police barricades in Delhi. Photo by Biplob Kumar Das for Drop Site News.
Many of those who responded to the CJP's call to action were out on the streets on their way to Jantar Mantar when Dipke and others were detained in the flight. Unable to reach the protest site, they wandered around the city. "Everytime the police stopped us on our way here, we told them we are tourists who are lost, so they let us pass by," said Shubham Sharma, 22, who was there with his 20-year-old cousin, Harsh.
Multiple journalists were detained, despite wearing their press badges. Lawyers were detained as well, including senior Supreme Court advocate Shadan Farasat, who was carried by his arms and legs to a police station. Overall, police detained over 2,000 protestors on Saturday, reported [Reuters](https://substack.com/redirect/7bea8090-0d95-4965-9386-13fc92557a9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Among those detained was the distinguished welfare economist Jean Dreze, who is originally from Belgium but has lived in India for nearly five decades, working on issues of poverty. "In almost 50 years of being in India, I have never seen such use of force to quell protests," Dreze told Drop Site from the police station.
Another protestor, 40-year-old Maalvi Mishra said that even as she was entering the lane to get to the protest site, she was told by the police that "Jantar Mantar is not in Delhi," and that she should go home. "I managed to come here but so many others couldn't," she said, as she held up a copy of the constitution in her hands, surrounded by cops and border security forces all around.
As protesters began entering the neighboring areas, police detained anyone who appeared to be heading towards the protest site.
"I reached Delhi from Punjab early in the morning and have been here since," said Karan Singh, who had travelled alone to attend the protests. "It was incredibly difficult to reach here, I had to walk for almost an hour. The police presence in the area makes it feel like it's fully a dictatorship," he said.

Drop Site saw protestors being detained within minutes of chanting slogans, or as soon as they merely came close to the barricaded roads outside Jantar Mantar. It wasn't just protestors--many were picked up from far beyond the protest premises, from arbitrary spots in the city, without explanation. "I didn't know anything about the protest, I am in the city for some work with my wife. The police just whisked me away without informing me why," said Mohammad Rahim, who was detained along with nearly 40 others in front of the New Delhi Railway Station.
In addition to the brute force applied by security forces, members of the right-wing Hindu Raksha Dal (Hindu Protection Force), who mobilized in support of the Narendra Modi government, were seen harassing some protestors. In a video that's now gone viral, four men were seen attacking a man and a woman, beating them up, with the police not intervening to stop them. The four were [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/4f84ecb9-a5be-43bf-b1f8-4b9a58b3482e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Sunday.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/01024d47-9aa9-4718-9ad4-f338d815104e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Security personnel detain demonstrators during a protest demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter roll irregularities, near Jantar Mantar in Delhi on October 11, 2026. Photo by Sajjad HUSSAIN / AFP via Getty Images.
## Protests Despite Crackdown
As crackdowns against protestors continued unabated, spontaneous demonstrations erupted in other parts of the city. A popular market for tourists called Dilli Haat suddenly emerged as the go-to spot as left wing student leader Neha Bora announced that as their choice of protest ground. A few hours later, the Safdarjung flyover, an extremely busy overpass in the heart of South Delhi, became another hot spot. The protests, however, could only occur in bursts, as people were being detained within minutes.
"Till the time there is even one person protesting on the street, this movement will continue," said Bora in a video message on social media. Bora pleaded with supporters to protest wherever the police tried to detain them.
Even as the largely young, Gen Z protestors were being bundled into police buses and vans, some from the older generations came to show solidarity and support.
Hansraj Bhutani, 82, came out into the street with food and water in his bag. "I am here to support the protestors," he said. "I have lived through the Emergency under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. Even then, things weren't this bad. I am requesting Modi to stop troubling the public like this."
In Connaught Place, a central market in Delhi, hundreds of protestors trying to make their way to Jantar Mantar were detained. The police presence in the area heavily outnumbered the protestors. The government prohibited the gathering of more than five people in central Delhi.
Many protestors, who had walked in alone, found solidarity with the few others who managed to make it past the barricades.
Papri Das, Pavneet Kaur, and Rosy met each other at the Connaught Place market while heading towards the protest site. "It is disheartening to see how the government is seeking to silence our voices. But what is heartening is that people are still showing up, despite the crackdowns and despite the police brutality," said Das, 34.
For Kaur, 35, the solidarity she found among each other gave her hope that this movement could be successful. "We just realized that the three of us belong to different religions. I am Sikh, Papri is Hindu, and Rosy is Muslim. This is exactly what the government fears--people becoming united to fight its tyranny," she said.
Not far from Connaught Place, police entered a Sikh temple, the Gurudwara Bangla Sahib, and detained people en masse. "I witnessed at least a dozen people being brutalized while the Delhi police tried to detain them. One 75-year-old woman was brutalized by the police so badly, one of her fingers was dangling off, we had to get her a plastic surgery," said a doctor who was offering medical relief to the injured inside the Gurudwara and did not want to be named out of fear of retaliation.
He said that the police entered the temple premises in their boots and without wearing a head scarf--as required of men entering Sikh places of worship. "Most people were injured due to the police twisting their fingers while trying to detain them. I saw a lot of pinching and nail marks on injured protestors. They are not using batons, but using these other means to brutalize protestors," he said.
The protests continued on Sunday, with spontaneous marches emerging in Connaught Place multiple times throughout the day and the police detaining hundreds of protestors. "I have been detained almost every day since October 2. I will continue to protest this regime and I will continue to show up on protest sites every day, there is no fear anymore," one protester told Drop Site through a window of a police bus.
## Support Networks
In response to the July protests, a citizen-led volunteer group began to take shape. The group, which calls itself the Protest Support Initiative, has multiple wings, each catering to a different aspect of providing aid and support, with about 150 volunteers. One wing is in charge of driving people home after they are let go from their detention centers, often in far-flung places. Another, led by doctors, is in charge of providing first-aid. There's also a wing of therapists who help people who've undergone trauma during the detention or during confrontation with the police.
For Meghnad, a popular journalist and content creator, forming the group seemed like the most natural thing to do. "No one else was doing it, but someone had to. So might as well be us," he said. "Eighteen year olds would come up to me asking how do we get home after the police leave us in random parts of the city after detention, I had to help them. I also realized many of these young protesters come from extremely repressive environments at home. They've found a space to express themselves through these protests, so we have to be there for them."

Until October 9, the group had 20 people who had volunteered to drive detainees home. After the October 10 protests, that number has risen to 93. But along with all the support, they now also face the scrutiny and intimidation that comes from the authorities. "Three people were following me throughout the protests on 10th. I routinely get a call from Delhi police checking on me," said Meghnad.
Satvik Soni, a filmmaker co-leading the Protest Support Initiative, said he had over 140,000 followers on Instagram before the government banned his account in India.
Soni said there was an "organizational gap" in how the protests were being mobilized, and that he and Meghnad have spent over 2 lakh rupees, or $2,600, from their own savings to provide aid to protesters.
"Two things need to happen for people to join the protests in large numbers," said Soni. "The CJP and other activists have made it cool to attend the protest. But someone needs to make it safe as well, and I think that's where we come in."

He said the last round of CJP-led protests, which led to the resignation of the Education Minister, left many protestors detained or injured in its wake. "The protestors had been stranded, and they were chased by right-wing goons and Delhi police," Soni said. "The leaders left, so we had to step in."

This is essential to our mission: to report on what matters most, beholden only to the truth. In that spirit, we made a commitment to ensure that our journalism is free for everyone, not locked behind a paywall. But that means we rely on the voluntary support of our community of readers. Please consider making a. | | ---|---|--- Demonstrators shout slogans during a protest demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter roll irregularities, near Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on October 11, 2026. Photo by Sajjad HUSSAIN / AFP via Getty Images. DELHI, India--Indian authorities enforced an unprecedented crackdown on demonstrations across Delhi on Saturday and Sunday, as student groups and citizen networks, including lawyers and doctors organized to provide support for people protesting a massive purge of voter lists. The government deployed over 20,000 police and paramilitary personnel to prevent protestors from gathering in the city, pulling forces from border areas, including Kashmir, into Delhi. For the past two weeks, protestors across India have been demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, after an investigation by The Indian Express, a prominent daily, revealed that the country's election commission had deleted more than 130 million people from voter rolls without due process. The call for large demonstrations on Saturday was made by the (CJP), which in July led widespread protests against the education minister Dharmendra Pradhan for irregularities in nationwide examinations, leading to his resignation. On Saturday, Delhi police detained Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of CJP, along with several other leaders of the group, on their airplane when they arrived at the Delhi airport, holding them until Sunday morning. The mobilization was supposed to be held at the designated protest site of Jantar Mantar, but it was entirely barricaded by the police, and most of central Delhi was under police lockdown. | | ---|---|--- Police barricades in Delhi. Photo by Biplob Kumar Das for Drop Site News. Many of those who responded to the CJP's call to action were out on the streets on their way to Jantar Mantar when Dipke and others were detained in the flight. Unable to reach the protest site, they wandered around the city. "Everytime the police stopped us on our way here, we told them we are tourists who are lost, so they let us pass by," said Shubham Sharma, 22, who was there with his 20-year-old cousin, Harsh. Multiple journalists were detained, despite wearing their press badges. Lawyers were detained as well, including senior Supreme Court advocate Shadan Farasat, who was carried by his arms and legs to a police station. Overall, police detained over 2,000 protestors on Saturday, reported . Among those detained was the distinguished welfare economist Jean Dreze, who is originally from Belgium but has lived in India for nearly five decades, working on issues of poverty. "In almost 50 years of being in India, I have never seen such use of force to quell protests," Dreze told Drop Site from the police station. Another protestor, 40-year-old Maalvi Mishra said that even as she was entering the lane to get to the protest site, she was told by the police that "Jantar Mantar is not in Delhi," and that she should go home. "I managed to come here but so many others couldn't," she said, as she held up a copy of the constitution in her hands, surrounded by cops and border security forces all around. As protesters began entering the neighboring areas, police detained anyone who appeared to be heading towards the protest site. "I reached Delhi from Punjab early in the morning and have been here since," said Karan Singh, who had travelled alone to attend the protests. "It was incredibly difficult to reach here, I had to walk for almost an hour. The police presence in the area makes it feel like it's fully a dictatorship," he said. Drop Site saw protestors being detained within minutes of chanting slogans, or as soon as they merely came close to the barricaded roads outside Jantar Mantar. It wasn't just protestors--many were picked up from far beyond the protest premises, from arbitrary spots in the city, without explanation. "I didn't know anything about the protest, I am in the city for some work with my wife. The police just whisked me away without informing me why," said Mohammad Rahim, who was detained along with nearly 40 others in front of the New Delhi Railway Station. In addition to the brute force applied by security forces, members of the right-wing Hindu Raksha Dal (Hindu Protection Force), who mobilized in support of the Narendra Modi government, were seen harassing some protestors. In a video that's now gone viral, four men were seen attacking a man and a woman, beating them up, with the police not intervening to stop them. The four were on Sunday. | | ---|---|--- Security personnel detain demonstrators during a protest demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter roll irregularities, near Jantar Mantar in Delhi on October 11, 2026. Photo by Sajjad HUSSAIN / AFP via Getty Images. Protests Despite Crackdown As crackdowns against protestors continued unabated, spontaneous demonstrations erupted in other parts of the city. A popular market for tourists called Dilli Haat suddenly emerged as the go-to spot as left wing student leader Neha Bora announced that as their choice of protest ground. A few hours later, the Safdarjung flyover, an extremely busy overpass in the heart of South Delhi, became another hot spot. The protests, however, could only occur in bursts, as people were being detained within minutes. "Till the time there is even one person protesting on the street, this movement will continue," said Bora in a video message on social media. Bora pleaded with supporters to protest wherever the police tried to detain them. Even as the largely young, Gen Z protestors were being bundled into police buses and vans, some from the older generations came to show solidarity and support. Hansraj Bhutani, 82, came out into the street with food and water in his bag. "I am here to support the protestors," he said. "I have lived through the Emergency under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. Even then, things weren't this bad. I am requesting Modi to stop troubling the public like this." In Connaught Place, a central market in Delhi, hundreds of protestors trying to make their way to Jantar Mantar were detained. The police presence in the area heavily outnumbered the protestors. The government prohibited the gathering of more than five people in central Delhi. Many protestors, who had walked in alone, found solidarity with the few others who managed to make it past the barricades. Papri Das, Pavneet Kaur, and Rosy met each other at the Connaught Place market while heading towards the protest site. "It is disheartening to see how the government is seeking to silence our voices. But what is heartening is that people are still showing up, despite the crackdowns and despite the police brutality," said Das, 34. For Kaur, 35, the solidarity she found among each other gave her hope that this movement could be successful. "We just realized that the three of us belong to different religions. I am Sikh, Papri is Hindu, and Rosy is Muslim. This is exactly what the government fears--people becoming united to fight its tyranny," she said. Not far from Connaught Place, police entered a Sikh temple, the Gurudwara Bangla Sahib, and detained people en masse. "I witnessed at least a dozen people being brutalized while the Delhi police tried to detain them. One 75-year-old woman was brutalized by the police so badly, one of her fingers was dangling off, we had to get her a plastic surgery," said a doctor who was offering medical relief to the injured inside the Gurudwara and did not want to be named out of fear of retaliation. He said that the police entered the temple premises in their boots and without wearing a head scarf--as required of men entering Sikh places of worship. "Most people were injured due to the police twisting their fingers while trying to detain them. I saw a lot of pinching and nail marks on injured protestors. They are not using batons, but using these other means to brutalize protestors," he said. The protests continued on Sunday, with spontaneous marches emerging in Connaught Place multiple times throughout the day and the police detaining hundreds of protestors. "I have been detained almost every day since October 2. I will continue to protest this regime and I will continue to show up on protest sites every day, there is no fear anymore," one protester told Drop Site through a window of a police bus. Support Networks In response to the July protests, a citizen-led volunteer group began to take shape. The group, which calls itself the Protest Support Initiative, has multiple wings, each catering to a different aspect of providing aid and support, with about 150 volunteers. One wing is in charge of driving people home after they are let go from their detention centers, often in far-flung places. Another, led by doctors, is in charge of providing first-aid. There's also a wing of therapists who help people who've undergone trauma during the detention or during confrontation with the police. For Meghnad, a popular journalist and content creator, forming the group seemed like the most natural thing to do. "No one else was doing it, but someone had to. So might as well be us," he said. "Eighteen year olds would come up to me asking how do we get home after the police leave us in random parts of the city after detention, I had to help them. I also realized many of these young protesters come from extremely repressive environments at home. They've found a space to express themselves through these protests, so we have to be there for them." Until October 9, the group had 20 people who had volunteered to drive detainees home. After the October 10 protests, that number has risen to 93. But along with all the support, they now also face the scrutiny and intimidation that comes from the authorities. "Three people were following me throughout the protests on 10th. I routinely get a call from Delhi police checking on me," said Meghnad. Satvik Soni, a filmmaker co-leading the Protest Support Initiative, said he had over 140,000 followers on Instagram before the government banned his account in India. Soni said there was an "organizational gap" in how the protests were being mobilized, and that he and Meghnad have spent over 2 lakh rupees, or $2,600, from their own savings to provide aid to protesters. "Two things need to happen for people to join the protests in large numbers," said Soni. "The CJP and other activists have made it cool to attend the protest. But someone needs to make it safe as well, and I think that's where we come in." He said the last round of CJP-led protests, which led to the resignation of the Education Minister, left many protestors detained or injured in its wake. "The protestors had been stranded, and they were chased by right-wing goons and Delhi police," Soni said. "The leaders left, so we had to step in." | A guest post by| Kumar Das is an investigative reporter covering politics and business, with a focus on institutional accountability and immigrant communities. I spent 40 years in uniform. I know the difference between sharing a burden and using the people beneath you as a backdrop. In Congress, I will force leaders like Hegseth to answer for the orders they sign and the damage they leave behind. During this deployment, the Navy told lawmakers that eight sailors attempted suicide. Families waited nearly eleven months for their loved ones to come home. [**Will you chip in $14 --one dollar for every county in GA-14--to help elect a commander who will hold Pete Hegseth accountable?**](http://clicksp.shawnharrisforcongress.com/f/a/RAWiFh6_SL1Vjrgp76MX9Q~~/AAPPABA~/ffz8SH50PY_4waIZLhwFt07moDcEgueCQT1fnbuL1_xOBsHAncd696fTTc80LAI5axnPDzqmGrpjf-eyo0HlsDoCDzxoFtTi8zPpoz_wB49-odicH8v54N1Gkdqt9aOaOAAhwi_0Ue6mz1WSpyGVEVEx939ZKthbV8yogxJlrgXP45bgMHfvXzwvStRKRlRtqpFQjO1XNC60i99Mbvt6a2Bm50QmWKw8RLe5JLEpGKD69_mX-qXPv9DfQRWuq57xecY7Qedr_8nqSTQzBw2mBVCUnSQ4ysKslRrM56IZ_03H_F3mSW3kO-o5okxbsjyZ) **Hegseth did not carry that burden. The sailors did.** He signed the extensions. They missed birthdays, anniversaries, and months with their children. Then he arrived at the finish line and talked about their toughness as if their suffering proved his leadership. **It proved the opposite.** Real commanders own the consequences of their decisions. They do not pose beside exhausted troops and call the damage "resilience." | | Peter,

Today is National Coming Out Day, so I want to tell you the story of how I decided to come out.

In the fall of 1990, I was a junior at Duke and a member of Alpha Epsilon Pi, the historically Jewish fraternity I'd pledged as a freshman. This was Durham, North Carolina, at the height of the AIDS crisis. I wasn’t sure how my fraternity brothers would react when they learned I was gay. Would they cast me out?

I decided to tell them anyway. Two months later, they elected me the president of our fraternity.

That moment of radical acceptance made a huge impression on me.

It’s part of what inspired my dedication to increasing equity and inclusion in our communities. Now, I’m running to be the first openly LGBTQ person ever elected to represent San Francisco in Congress.

Today, I’m asking for your support to reach voters with my record of results for our community. Breaking news, Peter:
**A brand-new GOP dark money group just poured over $1 million into defeating 6 of our endorsed candidates in critical state legislative races across the country.**
They’re coming after **Ruwa Romman** (GA-SD-7), **Kristian Carranza** (TX-HD-118), **Julio Salinas** (TX-HD-41), **Trevor Jung** (WI-SD-21), **Brad Chambers** (PA-HD-41), and **Tim Hayes** (PA-HD-143).

Let me be really clear about what’s happening here.
**Republicans have been quietly pouring money into state legislative races for decades.** Flipping chambers across the country, flooding statehouses with policies that attack our rights and make our lives harder, and then drawing rigged maps to lock in their power at every ballot level.
We’re still living with that impact. The GOP has used those supermajorities to enact abortion bans, gut public school funding, block Medicaid expansion for families who desperately need it, and make it harder to vote.
**That’s why our work of shining the spotlight on state legislative races and investing in down-ballot races is so critical.**
And in these tight races that could be decided by a handful of votes, this level of spending is the difference between breaking the GOP’s grip on power and watching them lock it in for another cycle.
We can’t let that happen.
**[So I’m asking you, Peter: will you pitch in $5 today to make sure our candidates can break through the noise and win in November?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261011_1_gop.KeTAlI&refcode=em20261011-4131&amount=5&t=3&akid=4131%2E587540%2Ea2R2m7)**

Thank you for your support.
— David Hogg

name: Danielle
subject: Where your dollar goes in the final weeks
body:
Dollars go further right now than at almost any other point in the race

| |
---
Friend, As Finance Director, I spend a lot of my day looking at one question: what can we do with the resources we have, and how much more could we do with a little extra? In the final weeks of a campaign, the answer to that question changes fast. Dollars go further right now than at almost any other point in the race, because nearly all of it goes straight to reaching voters. Thank you, thank you, thank you.

First, I just want to tell you how grateful I am that you even opened this email. This close to Election Day, I know you’re probably getting a lot of messages, so I truly appreciate your time.

This team always has my back. When the top super PACs try to drown us out, you step up. When we’re nearing a critical deadline, you help us reach our goal.

Thanks to the pressure we’ve built, Jon Husted is the #1 most vulnerable senator this election season. And because of this grassroots team, we have a chance to win this in the final sprint.

**But right now, we’re facing our very last FEC deadline in 72 hours, and if we want to win in 23 days, we’ve got to knock our $2.5 million goal out of the park.**

This $2.5 million will help us keep up with historic Republican spending. And to be frank, this is a seat we have to flip to have any chance at making our country work for working people again.

name: Aaron Ford
subject: A Skor bar
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford
body:
# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=1063%2E127862%2E0EeEp-)
We're four weeks from Election Day, and I'm running in one of the closest governor's races in the country.
I'll be honest with you: I never would’ve imagined I'd be in this position.
When I was a kid, my dad worked at a Safeway, and my mom worked odd jobs. They were hard workers, but we still struggled. I distinctly remember a night when all my brother and I had for dinner was a stale Skor bar.
That’s why I keep a Skor bar in my office to this day. Not to eat, but to serve as a reminder of where I come from. I don't ever want to forget.
I got to be where I am today because of government programs like food stamps and Medicaid. They uplifted my family out of tough situations.
**That's what happens when government invests in people. It didn't just change my life, it changed my family's.**
I couldn't sit back and watch as MAGA Republicans gut the same programs that had an immeasurable impact on my family. And I won't sit back while MAGA Gov. Joe Lombardo asks for four more years after telling Nevadans they need to "feel a little pain" from Trump's tariffs.
**I'm running because Nevada families deserve a governor who fights for them.** I’ll work to lower costs, protect Medicaid, and invest in Nevada families the way our government once invested in mine.
**The polls show we can win, but a race this close comes down to who has the resources to finish strong, and I need your support in the final stretch.**
**[If you're with me, will you chip in $5 today to help us cross the finish line?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261011_2_ak.LAi4yB&amount=5&refcode=em20261011-1048&t=3&akid=1063%2E127862%2E0EeEp-)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261011_2_ak.LAi4yB&amount=5&refcode=em20261011-1048&t=22&akid=1063%2E127862%2E0EeEp-)**
With gratitude,
Aaron

Friends,
The final FEC deadline before the election is on Oct. 14 at 11:59 p.m. That's just around the corner, and I'll be honest: This is a make-or-break moment for our campaign. Let me explain.
Right now, polls show me with a razor-thin lead over Roger Marshall. Multiple election forecasters -- from Nate Silver to Cook Political Report and even Steve Kornacki -- have shifted this race to a toss-up. And Roll Call officially named Roger Marshall one of the most vulnerable senators in the country.
That's all really good news. But here's the not-so-good news: The latest polls show this race is tightening. Roger Marshall and his allies are going all out to crush our momentum. In fact, the GOP's top super PAC just launched a _massive_ ad buy to drown us out and turn voters against me right as early voting in Kansas gets underway.
That brings me to the FEC deadline. We've set a goal of raising $2,000,000 by 11:59 p.m. on Oct. 14. _That 's just three days from now. _If we fall short of our target, Marshall and his supporters will think we're vulnerable -- and they'll almost certainly up their spend and their attacks even more than they already have.
With the first Kansans starting to cast their ballots on Oct. 14, we need to reach our goal to keep our ads on the air, fight back against the super PAC's attack ads and reach every voter we can.
Friends, everything we raise by the FEC deadline will be a matter of public record, so we absolutely cannot slow down now. Sen. Marshall and his allies are pouring everything into this race because they know it's going to come down to the wire. They didn't expect that. For the last 94 years, every Kansas U.S. Senator has come from the same political party. They didn't think a first-time candidate with a grassroots campaign built around bringing people together instead of tearing them apart could win this.
**But we can. We must.**
Kansans deserve better than another six years of Roger Marshall rubber-stamping policies that cut their healthcare, make it harder to buy groceries and drive up the price of gas. They deserve a leader who will work to build bridges, listen to their problems and fight to make their lives better.
**This final FEC deadline before the election is a chance to send that message loud and clear to Sen. Marshall and his allies one last time before voters go to the polls. Most of all, it 's a chance to show them the true strength of our incredible grassroots movement. Because make no mistake: They'll be watching.**
**[I know we can win this, but we need a surge of grassroots support to get us across the finish line. The stakes couldn't be higher. So please, pitch in $5, $10 or whatever you can right now to help us reach our final FEC fundraising goal of the race, turn out every supporter and flip this seat?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/9822e037-9a0e-4235-b7bc-8f47fcbc9b23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/9822e037-9a0e-4235-b7bc-8f47fcbc9b23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for all you do,
Adam

Let me explain. Right now, polls show me with a razor-thin lead over Roger Marshall. Multiple election forecasters -- from Nate Silver to Cook Political Report and even Steve Kornacki -- have shifted this race to a toss-up. And Roll Call officially named Roger Marshall one of the most vulnerable senators in the country. That's all really good news. But here's the not-so-good news: The latest polls show this race is tightening. Roger Marshall and his allies are going all out to crush our momentum. In fact, the GOP's top super PAC just launched a massive ad buy to drown us out and turn voters against me right as early voting in Kansas gets underway. That brings me to the FEC deadline. We've set a goal of raising $2,000,000 by 11:59 p.m. on Oct. 14. That 's just three days from now. If we fall short of our target, Marshall and his supporters will think we're vulnerable -- and they'll almost certainly up their spend and their attacks even more than they already have. With the first Kansans starting to cast their ballots on Oct. 14, we need to reach our goal to keep our ads on the air, fight back against the super PAC's attack ads and reach every voter we can. Friends, everything we raise by the FEC deadline will be a matter of public record, so we absolutely cannot slow down now. Sen. Marshall and his allies are pouring everything into this race because they know it's going to come down to the wire. They didn't expect that. For the last 94 years, every Kansas U.S. Senator has come from the same political party. They didn't think a first-time candidate with a grassroots campaign built around bringing people together instead of tearing them apart could win this. But we can. We must. Kansans deserve better than another six years of Roger Marshall rubber-stamping policies that cut their healthcare, make it harder to buy groceries and drive up the price of gas. They deserve a leader who will work to build bridges, listen to their problems and fight to make their lives better. This final FEC deadline before the election is a chance to send that message loud and clear to Sen. Marshall and his allies one last time before voters go to the polls. Most of all, it 's a chance to show them the true strength of our incredible grassroots movement. Because make no mistake: They'll be watching. Thank you for all you do, Adam | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Adam Hamilton for Kansas 548 Market Street PMB 72296, San Francisco, CA 94104 ? ?

It's not a fluke, either. This is the third poll showing us ahead of Abbott, and it's the most recent one, taken after weeks of Abbott's attack ads flooding Texas airwaves. [**Split $25 right now between Equal Opportunity Now****and my campaign to help us turn this polling lead into a win.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141204968/652785543/1593610140?amount=25&refcode=261011_gina_nytpoll&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlOGZmOTc2Zi1hNmM1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=S1dFBJ1DLR2gK4HQEDT6yucuwDUxuZqlbFg2biRkG_I=) The _New York Times_ also ran a major story on the state of play in Texas. clean_body: Three fights that may not have made headlines, but mattered. | Peter – Some of Washington’s most important wins this year haven’t made national headlines. In August, my office helped stop the Trump administration from cutting federal housing funds that Washington communities rely on. Without that victory, nearly 3,000 Washingtonians could have lost their homes. A few weeks later, we helped protect federal funding that supports fair-housing enforcement across our state. That funding helps Washington investigate housing discrimination and make sure people have a fair chance to find a home. And last month, we reached a settlement that protected more than $21 million in AmeriCorps funding for Washington. Those programs support communities across our state and give people opportunities to serve where they live. These fights may not be the ones you see on the news. But they matter. Twice in the Last 100 Years, Washington Changed What a Dollar Is. Both Times, Most People Found Out Too Late.
In 1933 and in 1971, the rules of American money were rewritten almost overnight. Savers lost. Owners of the right assets won big. Now the plumbing of the dollar is being rebuilt again, and almost nobody is paying attention.

Money feels permanent. The bills in your wallet, the balance in your account, the number on your retirement statement. But the rules behind that money have been rewritten before, by a handful of officials, with very little warning. And each time, the gap between people who saw it coming and people who didn’t became enormous.
The evidence board
| | The Last Two Resets
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**1933.** In April, President Roosevelt signed Executive Order 6102, requiring Americans to hand over most of their gold to the Federal Reserve at $20.67 an ounce. Months later, Washington raised the official price to $35. Anyone holding dollars instead of gold had effectively lost about 40% of their purchasing power against it.
| EVIDENCE
---
**1971.** On a Sunday evening in August, President Nixon cut the dollar’s last link to gold. It was announced as temporary. It was never reversed. Prices have risen more than eightfold since then, while people who owned real assets saw their wealth multiply.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Now.** In July 2025, President Trump signed the GENIUS Act, the first federal law for dollar-backed digital tokens. By June 2026, that market was worth about $270 billion. Brookings estimates it could create $400 billion to $2.3 trillion in new demand for U.S. Treasury bills by 2030.
Why it matters to you
| | What a Reset Does to Ordinary Savers
---|---
| →| **It doesn’t ask permission.** Neither 1933 nor 1971 went to a public vote. Both took effect almost immediately.
---|---
| →| **It moves wealth, not just prices.** Each time, cash savers fell behind while owners of the right assets pulled ahead.
---|---
| →| **The early movers win.** Those who understood the change before it was obvious kept, and often grew, their wealth.
---|---

| | The Official Line
---|---
| | “The dollar is our currency, but it’s your problem.”— U.S. Treasury Secretary John Connally, 1971
---|---
What it says
Washington will run the dollar to suit Washington.
What it means
**Our theory:** that hasn’t changed. What’s changing is the machinery. The government now has a new channel to sell its debt and new rails for dollars to travel on. Changes like that don’t stay technical for long. They end up in your grocery bill, your savings rate and the value of everything you own.

The headlines treat this as a niche crypto story. It isn’t. It’s a change in how dollars are created, moved and backed, and history says the winners of a monetary shift are decided early.

It’s a beautiful idea. It’s also a dangerous one to plan your life around. No one, including Musk, can say when that future arrives. Your rent, insurance and groceries are due this month.

| EVIDENCE

**Exhibit C — what income investors do instead.** Partnerships that own pipelines and storage, the energy infrastructure the country runs on, are a classic source of steady income. A widely held fund that tracks them yields around 8%, and its May 2026 payout was a record.

It’s important. The last FEC filing deadline of this election is right around the corner, and unfortunately, we’re not raising what we need each day to reach our ambitious goal. Hitting this goal is the only way we can stay on track to flip North Carolina – the seat Democrats must win to have any chance of retaking Senate control and stopping President Trump. I know you can’t donate to every email I send, but I’m asking you to give to this one. The GOP has poured millions into false attack ads against me, and my ability to fight back depends on grassroots support from people like you. Will you please chip in? My team and I are tracking donations at this link: Thank you so much. Roy | | Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here. National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us. Earlier this year, I sat down with a podcaster who asked me my favorite taco order. I let them know what I order often depends on where I'm at. If I'm in Central Texas, it's potato and egg. When I'm in the Rio Grande Valley, I'm getting barbacoa. In El Paso, I'm having something with chile colorado. When I'm at home, I'm simply having tortilla con aguacate because it brings me back to my grandmother and my childhood home.
The diversity of Texas' taco orders is a direct parallel to the diversity of the needs of our great state region to region. In rural Texas, communities are being forced to fight back against data center giants. In areas like Corpus, communities faced months of not knowing if they'd run out of water. In West Texas along the border, activists have come together to fight back against the destruction of Big Bend.
Regardless of those differences, we are all fighting for the same thing -- a chance to achieve the American dream. For me that has always meant well funded neighborhood public schools, access to healthcare, and a chance to buy a home and maybe take a vacation from time to time. Under Greg Abbott, Texans are struggling to realize this dream.
For over 30 years Greg Abbott has put his donors ahead of hardworking Texans to stay in power. This year's election is our chance to put an end to sweetheart deals and under the table negotiations. Texans deserve a Governor who will be transparent and committed to bettering the lives of all Texans -- not just those with money and influence.
**Whether in Dallas or down in the Valley, my vision for the people of Texas remains steadfast. Strengthen public schools so every child in Texas has a good quality education, and ensure public school teachers are among the highest paid in the nation. Lower living costs and help working families keep more of their hard-earned money. Protect our water and power grid by putting real guardrails on unchecked data centers. Hold health insurance companies accountable and ensure Texans have access to quality healthcare.**
I launched this race knowing that I was running against an incumbent with a three decade political career mired with corruption. I ran on the hopes that people would believe in my vision for a better Texas, and with four polls showing me _leading_ against Greg Abbott in the Texas Governor's race, I am glad to not be in this fight alone.
Winning this race is not going to be an easy feat. We are nearly one week away from early voting, and November 3rd will be here before we know it. My race against Abbott would not have the momentum we do if not for supporters like you.
**[Thank you for showing up for me, but we're not done fighting yet. If you can, will you please chip in $5 or whatever you can today to help keep our ads on air, and support the voter outreach we are still doing, and will be doing up until the polls close?](https://substack.com/redirect/50a0501f-7b73-4995-8f18-bd0bf2a9c9f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE ->](https://substack.com/redirect/50a0501f-7b73-4995-8f18-bd0bf2a9c9f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Our taco orders may be different, but our fight for a better Texas is one in the same.
-- Gina

# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241115%2E444211%2EKfknA3)
A student at UNT recently asked me, “Why are you doing this?”
I think she meant: you're not on the ballot, you're not in office. So what are you still doing out here? I told her the truth – this work makes me feel useful.
It's what keeps me going and keeps me up when otherwise I'd be down. Here's what "this" looks like.
Our volunteers get certified and trained, then head to campuses, coffee shops, and concerts across Texas – meeting young people where they are and personally staying in touch with every one of them to make sure they vote.
And it works. In 2024, young voters in our program turned out at 79%. The statewide average: 39%. The alternative – hoping someone else will do it while we wait on the sidelines – is unthinkable.

Friends,
**After Trump announced federal monitors will be going to the polls on Election Day, Democratic Secretaries of State have been actively planning out all potential scenarios of federal interference.**
Federal law prohibits voter intimidation and bars “troops or armed men” from being deployed at polling locations. Our elections are supposed to be free from fear, coercion, and intimidation.
**Here’s a few examples of what our election officials are doing to protect our poll workers and voters:**
🔻 DASS Chair and Nevada Sec. Cisco Aguilar said he is assembling “the Mad Libs of legal filings” in case of any and all election problems.
🔻 Local election officials in South Carolina and Arizona are gaming out responses to potential threats that would disrupt our elections – such as federal investigations.
**As a reminder, Trump said he’ll do anything to keep our elections “honest.”**

Peter, I need to be candid with you.
Our grassroots fundraising isn’t where it needs to be right now, and we’ve had to drop our October projections.
At the same time as we’re falling behind on our fundraising goals, the GOP’s lies and attacks against me are ramping up. They’ve poured tens of millions into this race to defeat me – because if we lose in North Carolina, Democrats will have no shot at taking back the Senate.
The only way we can protect our edge and keep powering forward is with a surge of grassroots support from people like you – so today, I’m trying something different. **I’m lowering my ask to just $1 in the hopes that every person reading this message chips in.**
While we have fundraising goals to hit, what matters most to me today is how many contributions we’re able to get in the door. Every dollar adds up fast when we’re all pitching in, and together, we can rebuild our momentum and show the strength of this grassroots movement.

That tells us something important: [**National Democrats see an opportunity in Western and Southern Colorado, and they are looking for the money to take advantage of it.**](http://idp_131_wi11p0217xkfu2tebdwany4z.jeffhurdforcolorado.com/ls/click?upn=u001.LskycFtCvn2sZGOv-2Fcl7zsTQ3vToy0CgKKAUn6qqpRYP9irRvtsXwf42fKrjhgO-2F2508ghRorMrwhpc1vwFpPiUeq5kiQK9-2BiLIBnkKBhQUW-2FdhDuMMpSXi2SSuRgekBisOTr5fev4x-2FsONfVcHo8DaeRq0S-2Bb5Xj3RdUSG54kAgT-2F4JlM2K1AGLykK4We92vuV6_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVDV5VGX0FZC332Dsse9-2FPZlI6OP-2Fj7E15boaB8t6wql59FOswEqORD0nJYDNtQTuOw7fFCxLMtWdK-2F8J-2BDh3-2BgbyINj8sab6OmMjoIz4-2FSw56-2B7vi3wYVz-2B6M5wazyTBvaGlMYOObdDPwAYxuHWtTVJ93r5KPQL3PGCCBzduZN3mTQENu-2FZFKpcewT1FExymJ15-2B3am9Nv2i6X7k1yN-2BP-2FRRtyz-2FG-2BvI3TV0Zegywf-2Fd8osy9FRoTMLlf3f1LmuhlNXl5ovQ0WH3P7t-2FGZxXiq-2F)

That has meant standing up to my own party when I believe it's wrong, working across the aisle to get legislation passed, and fighting for the water, energy, agriculture, and rural communities that make our district special.
I'm proud of that record, and I'm not going to change how I represent this district because of pressure from either political party.

Have you seen Greg Abbott's nasty ad about me yet, Peter?
He’s spending $35 million to blast his attack ads on the TV and radio airwaves across Texas.
**First of all, it’s a lie. Plain and simple.**
But there’s a reason he’s telling it. He doesn’t want Texans to know he’s about to raise our property taxes.
Abbott’s record is clear: Take over school districts, hand out vendor contracts to his donors, and raise property taxes. He did it in Houston; now it’s happening in Fort Worth and Beaumont – Austin could be next.
But unfortunately, that $35 million lie is how some Texans are meeting me for the very first time. If we let Abbott define me before they hear from us, that’s what they’ll take into the voting booth when polls open 8 days from now.
We're up on TV with our own ad, but it's only live where we can afford to run it. Every dollar we raise helps us put it in front of more Texans before they vote.

# 23 days...
### Get ready.
| | | [Brian Lenney](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)

---
| [](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)

The election day is 23 days out.
This year's Idaho ballot is loaded: drugs, English as the official state language, and abortion are up for grabs (just to name a few). Whoever shows up decides these, and I'd rather it be us.
And by "us" I mean America First conservatives. If you're a leftist, a Democrat, a drug loving open borders Libertarian, or some hack who got on my list to see what I'm up to, I'm not talking about you. You can feel free to sit this one out.
I wrote a letter to my district here in Nampa, and I think you should read it before you vote:

**» [Read the letter](https://substack.com/redirect/c1b578e4-be16-42ab-84f5-3ee6cf7a7353?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Vote early or vote on November 3.
Either way, bring a ton of people with you. Your spouse, your neighbors, your coworkers, the guy at church who keeps saying he'll "get around to it."
Drive them yourself if you have to.
The leftists aren't getting my state.
Cheers,
Brian

clean_body: We need to win by a cheating-proof margin. | | | At his desperate “Republican Midterm Convention,” Donald Trump led the crowd in a surprisingly revealing pledge: The Washington Post: “Trump asks convention crowd to pledge to him they will vote, ‘cheat like hell’” “I will go out with my family, my friends, I’ll do it any way, I don’t care if I’m registered or not, I’m going to try and cheat like hell...I am gonna go out, and I’m gonna get my friends, my family, and we are going to vote on November 3 or we are going to vote before that.” Telling his supporters to win an election by cheating? Sounds about right from the guy who tried to overturn 2020, who tries to suppress the vote so he can decide who casts a ballot, and who’s led the charge for extreme gerrymandering and rigged, racist voting maps. = Now, we can already hear the MAGA enablers trying to justify Trump’s comments. “He was just kidding!” they’ll say. “It was just a joke!” they’ll insist. But even if it was, there’s a kernel of truth behind every joke. Here’s the truth behind Trump’s assaults on democracy: he knows his party can’t win the 2026 midterm elections — as long as those elections are free and fair. They will cheat. We will vote. Peter, Reports out of south Texas say an Army soldier's wife named Giovanna showed up for a military ID appointment and left in ICE custody. She came to this country at age six and has four American-born kids. **Her husband Pedro is now expected to keep serving the government that just destroyed his family.** As my fellow Texas Democrat Bobby Pulido said, that's not law and order - that's betrayal.

This cruelty keeps happening to military families under Keith Self’s watch.
Back in April, ICE detained Deisy Rivera Ortega at an El Paso immigration appointment right after she handed over her military spouse ID.
Her husband has given the Army 27 years, Afghanistan included, and he watched agents cuff his wife without an explanation.
That same month, another military wife got detained at Fort Polk while filing her spouse paperwork.
A few weeks after that, a Marine veteran’s wife was taken at her green card meeting, and their baby daughter was at home when it happened
Texas military families keep going through hell, month after month, and Keith Self has not done a thing about it.
Keith Self is a retired Army officer. He knows firsthand what these families sacrifice.
Any officer worth anything would be pounding on the Secretary’s door, firing up congressional hearings, and introducing articles of impeachment over this conduct.
But Keith Self seems to have forgotten the people he once led – and today he only serves himself and Trump.

Maybe Keith Self is comfortable watching ICE haul off a soldier’s wife, but I’m not. In Congress, I will fight for accountability and oversight of ICE agents and their leadership when they break the law.
Our greatest patriots knew that devotion to this country sometimes means standing against the people running it.
Smedley Butler won the Medal of Honor twice, then spent his retirement calling out profiteers who misused the troops he loved.
Eisenhower won a world war, then used his farewell address to warn us about the perpetual war machine.
They loved this country enough to protect its people from its government when the government went wrong.
I spent 20 years in that uniform, and I am asking you to help me take this seat and fight for every family the extremists have thrown away.
[We have 23 days left to win this. Patriot,

At 23 years old, I was leading a remote combat outpost in Afghanistan's Arghandab Valley, responsible for over 350 personnel and $100 million in infrastructure and equipment.

**[That kind of pressure changes you. It taught me that accountability isn't optional, and that mission success depends on the people you lead — not the title you hold.](http://links.harriganfornc.com/u/click?_t=687026f8d8f7415aa539c5385c376b1f&_m=cf51bf87ac334d6c841e5528dde2321f&_e=myCTp98iZBoSuU1dTGPPU2bNTT3pH03WBfJM-w6ZhLqDwMVNebX-3qesiDqJS0D3P6kBMFL-4OMSMMAlVyw0MOSwGZxqPmvo2tvTmsAMOySmvVKJfWKMSIm1NTdg74ZGP9oTsJUO49Fqbeu797eFRNYps-k3OsFdSxPGLm-PnthJB9I8q0mIGIWNnqs7vcP2f5SracO1QDowToT5eG6cJ4z7nRxp9tvVCaISPJxvbonz3XzRuyT9kQjFQimf6tOq6eFoBdgIJsVq1sNDrG0011W2AODyQAp4RWImD08mf9mhdbX_lOl6Fva1esYDMmWoHo4ly4s40UlW9m2HFmQeE4G6X5wm3o-dps6z8oByTOcH_skQoZo421rS7g2Oe4Ir-XmLDTroBhiAmWF-WKVSpjeLtwQA4OJ5Xgoda6XIeyXHjwH_I6iNVvjgonyqOrSto6nQrbIci8L2K4zSIiC6O-rccClJ8h_JoQ-Rqxqh1n3ZBIYvcbuWZSkBny821v1R4hKO1fGxbRxF7-N1mkaOm5G_hhC4Qm3cMQygGs0C8WM%3D)**

I volunteered for the Green Berets because I recognized a need for greater expertise in unconventional warfare. I returned to Afghanistan with the Army Special Forces, led operations in some of the country's most volatile environments, and was awarded two Bronze Stars for that service.

clean_body: A story worth knowing before November | Backup requested. Send reinforcements. | | Patriot, At 23 years old, I was leading a remote combat outpost in Afghanistan's Arghandab Valley, responsible for over 350 personnel and $100 million in infrastructure and equipment. I volunteered for the Green Berets because I recognized a need for greater expertise in unconventional warfare. I returned to Afghanistan with the Army Special Forces, led operations in some of the country's most volatile environments, and was awarded two Bronze Stars for that service. | While I was still in uniform, my wife, Rocky, and I started a small firearms business out of our home. It grew from our living room into a manufacturing facility in Western North Carolina that creates real jobs for this region today. Then, I witnessed the absolute failure of bad leadership when President Biden allowed Afghanistan to fall -- and I knew I had to act. I'm a husband to Rocky, a dad to our two daughters, Reagan and McKinley, and I'm not done fighting for this district or for the country I love. But I can't keep fighting without your help. | | Dear Fellow American, Classic children's literature is being ignored and eliminated from our nation's classrooms at an alarming rate. Beloved classics like _The Wind in the Willows_ , _Treasure Island_ , and _The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn_ are just a few of the foundational books that are rarely being taught to our nation's children today. Not only does this rob young people of classic tales of adventure and friendship, but they also rob children of fundamental lessons about the world and how best to live.
---

# **MY FIRST TV ADS WILL BE ON AIR!**
In my previous campaigns, I never had enough money to run a single TV ad. This year, thanks to YOU, my grassroots supporters, we finally did it!

subject: Friend, I will never take you for granted
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Bobby Pulido for Texas
body:
Don't skip this email. It's not like the others in your inbox. |
---
[](https://eboq88hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001HVaB6_MVhaaI_ucTovTTRKDjgSz6Ua9a7ij-FQ0Td5QM198aOet-CvJgPKIxoFpci-Z5G8wwhdwkH9tVlX6m-ayIsQZiV-vt68rz2VQf2Oxr9wIhiv7arKpBMYkEcMibXiURIsH2yiBpYZ5r5ppjMDgQFJulpXky_BpPCscAatiKsdbS8ML0Ezek27cK_nJpz-hX2vir1wfdYrNhOX2l93cdher24ktcspb0rIYf5kzw33rIfBiL2X0tOGYae25GeoboPaxDBTIoBEREZfG6PVM4Em1F9XBCgc36L7fRWn8=&c=aKJG7MK2FHCZr3HLUJZHZ7AQZ7EKD1gNydwUZFAWqBsiXmKzVq4YTw==&ch=6OtR3JDad38TXOQmoOfPBkZZ_w2arjZw3PIVnZM1IIoaf7GISZmmog==)
Friend, I bet you're swamped with emails from candidates asking for $10 who don't even try to earn it. I know the value of your support, so I refuse to do that.Instead, I'm going to state plainly, right up front: _South Texas is worth fighting for._ I was blessed to have a career for 30 years in Tejano music, releasing albums and even winning a couple of Latin GRAMMY awards. But I gave it all up to run for Congress, and I'm going to tell you why.**South Texas gave me a voice. This community, my** _**gente,**_**they deserve a voice in Washington.** We've had enough of politicians like Monica De La Cruz who forget our community until election season comes around. We have folks down here who can't afford to pay their rent or mortgage or hospital bills, and it's met with utter silence by the people we entrust to do something about it.So I stepped up.One year later, TX-15 is the tipping-point race that could give Democrats control of Congress. | | | My name is Mary Peltola, and with just a few weeks until Election Day, I want to share with you why I made the decision to run for this Senate seat – and to ask for your support in this final stretch. **[But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and Equal Opportunity Now:](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141211206/652805281/916216164?refcode=261011_peltola_decision&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNWIyNDJiMi1jZGM1LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rqy6XjObddKwi_C9uKzzbXSICguoop5Bd3jIf2sWz08=)**

When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.

Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.

Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.

So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.

And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us.

They're focused on their own wallets – not ours.

And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.

It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.

I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.

My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning. But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.

I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future. This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.

So I am asking:

subject: FWD: More Hollywood donors line up for Annie Andrews
body:
The list is growing. |
Fellow Patriot - more Hollywood donors are lining up for my opponent.

This week, John Goodman sent out a fundraising text for my opponent.
